sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Why do sharp curves, slick asphalt, and standing puddles all demand immediate speed drops?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Sharp bends, slick pavement and pooled water all order slower speeds, since rubber meets road only through tire grip.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: How should you maintain your tires, and why must speed drop on gravel or dirt?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Keep tires sound and aired per the owner book, and crawl gravel and dirt where stops stretch and turns skid.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: When must you shed speed for a curve, and what happens if you brake mid-bend?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Shed speed before curves because mid bend braking breaks traction and sends cars sliding.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Why must all curve braking finish on the straightaway before turning in?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Curves want braking finished before entry, because braking inside the bend itself breaks grip and starts the skid.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: How must every driver treat an intersection whose traffic signals have gone dark?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Dead intersection signals legally become stop signs for every approaching driver.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: How much should you cut speed on wet pavement, packed snow, and glare ice?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: First rain, snow or sleet means ease off: drop ten miles per hour wet, halve speed on packed snow with snow tires or chains, and crawl ice or skip driving it.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: What three speed reductions match wet roads, packed snow with winter gear, and ice?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Wet roads cost ten miles per hour, packed snow halves speed with winter rubber, and ice demands a crawl or a cancelled trip.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Between which exact calendar dates are studded snow tires legal in Connecticut?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Studded tires stay legal in Connecticut from November fifteenth through April thirtieth.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How do snow tires and chains differ legally from studded tires across the calendar?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Snow tires and chains serve any snowfall, while studs stay legal only from November fifteenth through April thirtieth.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Which four sneaky spots or weather moments turn roads unexpectedly icy or oil-slick?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: Suspect ice in shady hollows, on uninsulated bridges, near freezing wetness, and during first minutes of hot day rain lifting asphalt oil.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Why do shady hollows, bridges, melting ice near freezing, and hot opening rain slide worst?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Shade freezes earliest and dries latest, bridges ice without earthen insulation, thaw edges slick most, and first hot rains float on risen oil.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: Above roughly what speed do wet tires start hydroplaning, and what makes it happen sooner?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: Wet tires grip only to about thirty five miles per hour before skimming water, sooner when bald, and downpours can float them fully, so slow down.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: What should your feet and hands do once your tires start hydroplaning on water?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Once floating, lift off the gas, steer straight with only slow emergency turns, and brake or steer solely after grip returns.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How do preventing hydroplaning near thirty-five miles per hour and curing it afloat work together?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: Tires swim near thirty five miles per hour in rain and sooner when worn, so prevention is slowing early while the cure afloat is lifting, straightening and waiting.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What deadly threat can aggressive driving grow into, and what mindset guards your license privilege?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Aggressive driving can ripen unknowingly into road rage with deadly fallout, so privilege demands self control behind the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: Which four social and traffic factors form the first group feeding road rage?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Rage feeds on jams, angry parent models, fading courtesy, and green youths rattled by tense moments.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Which four psychological traps make drivers treat lanes like personal turf and armor?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Rage also feeds on life stress spillover, claimed road territory, false armor feelings at speed, and cars mistaken for body extensions.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which calm habits defuse road rage before or after another motorist cuts you off?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Defuse by phoning police later not punishing now, refusing races, venting to riders, delaying angry trips or handing keys over, and granting blunderers the doubt of fatigue.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How should you report reckless aggression, and which roadside reactions are strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Aggressors earn a calm later call to police, never instant roadside punishment, competition, or weaponized retaliation.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What should you do with the keys when already angry, and how should mistakes be viewed?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Angry drivers should delay, delegate or taxi the trip, and grant offenders the doubt of fatigue rather than malice.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Which five obnoxious lane, signal, gesture, and horn habits spark road-rage confrontations?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Trouble brews from lane blocking, tailgating that sparks deadly fights, unsignaled cuts with stuck blinkers, rude fingers, and horn abuse including green light blasts.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: What danger links left-lane camping with tailgating, and what simple habits prevent both?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Camping the passing lane and tailgating both invite deadly fights, so yield left and keep real gaps.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What parking, headlight, merge, and roadway habits round out Connecticut's trouble-behavior list?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Trouble also brews from red light lane squatting, sloppy parking and handicap theft with door dings, high beam wars solved by dimming plus night four second gaps, merge hogging, trailer blocking and chatty road stands, and endless alarms.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: When is touching the horn appropriate, and which three uses abuse it?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: Horns serve rare light taps only, never greetings, green light blasts, or beam for beam revenge.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: How should you react to a hostile driver's glare, and where must you go if chased?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Deny hostile drivers eye contact and acknowledgment, and when chased flee to police posts or bright public stores, never home.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: What two things do you deny an angry driver, and what two places offer refuge?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Hostile drivers get no eyes and no answers, and pursuers get led to police posts or bright stores rather than home.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: How should you adjust space and lane position for trucks ahead, overtaking you, or oncoming?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.memory_hook: Extra room, ease pace, hug right
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Spare trucks their braking room ahead, ease off to help their passes without ever speeding up, and hug right past oncoming rigs against wind shove.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: How many counted thousands must separate you from a truck ahead at a roadside landmark?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Trail trucks by at least three counted thousands to a roadside mark, since closer means driving blind to them and for them.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: What five hidden hazards punish drivers who follow a large truck too closely?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Peeking left invites head on surprises, truck cleared debris still bites, rigs can outbrake cars, night high beams blind their mirrors, and upgrade stops need offset room against rollbacks.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Why do long trucks swing left before turning right, and where must you never squeeze?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Long rear wheels cut corners short, forcing trucks left before right bends, so never slip up a turning truck right side toward the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: How should you respond when a large truck starts backing into a dock or driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: Halt and gift backing trucks their swing room instead of circling around into invisibility and a needless crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How should you handle truck blinkers, vehicles merging off ramps, and multi-lane highway entries?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Honor truck slows and signals with patience, feed entering ramp traffic real gaps, and join highways through true openings without sweeping every lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What four habits apply around trucks at rail crossings, narrow roads, busy merges, and shoulders?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: Grant stopping trucks their rail crossings, cruise right on narrower roads, favor center lanes amid heavy merges, and shun shoulders always.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: Which two surprising truck behaviors demand wider following distance and ban curbside right passes?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Trucks can halt harder than cars despite their bulk, and their tails cheat inward on rights, so gaps grow and right side passes die.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: How should you use an entrance ramp to join highway traffic, and what if gaps close?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: Join traffic at its own speed with full ramp run ups, never halting ramp ends, and brake early on ramps when gaps force waiting.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How large a time opening does a safe merge require, and why reject smaller gaps?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Every merge wants a four second hole split two and two, and undersized holes only shrink further.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does the four-second merge opening compare with the normal dry-road following gap?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Joining traffic wants a four second hole shared two seconds each way, which is roomier than the three second trail kept once settled in line.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: Why does matching surrounding traffic speed beat weaving faster than everyone else?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Match surrounding pace because speed gaps breed crashes and passing gambles, while speeding banks just minutes per hour.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: When do you slow for a highway exit ramp versus a fast two-lane turnoff?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Hold main road pace until exit ramps, and brake late then briskly yet safely for fast two lane turnoffs with followers behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: What rules govern blocked intersections, narrow medians, turn signals, and railroad tracks when crossing traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Cross only through full clear widths, pause solely in fitting medians, keep left paths and greens truly open under ticket threat, trust no blinker until it turns, and never halt atop rails.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: May you enter a backed-up intersection on green, and when is stopping halfway legal?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Green lights still forbid entering blocked crossings under ticket threat, and halfway pauses survive solely inside vehicle fitting medians.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: How do you use a roadside object to verify you are not tailgating?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Gauge gaps by thousands from a fixed mark: arriving before three means tailing, so fall back and recount until three holds.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Which road, weather, or vehicle conditions require stretching your gap to four seconds?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Stretch to four seconds on slick roads, for passing neighbors, behind motorcycles, unseen tailers, trailers, dim sight, emergency rigs, halt bound crossings and hill stops, and cede right to tailgaters.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: When is three seconds enough ahead, and which hazards push your cushion to four?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Dry open roads need three counted seconds astern, while slick roads, trailers, dim sight, bikes, blind rigs and rail halts all stretch the gap to four.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How do you manage space behind your car and safely handle a close tailgater?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Guard rear room with steady pace and early signals, park pickups off road, telegraph parallel moves, yield slow lanes at turnouts, mirror every slowdown, and melt right or ease gently for tailgaters, never brake checking.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: What two calm moves clear a tailgater safely, and which retaliatory move causes wrecks?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Tailgaters earn a rightward cede or a gentle slow coaxing them past, and brake checking them back only courts a rear ender.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: How do you keep open side cushions around packs, parked doors, cyclists, and dual hazards?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Own side room by shunning packs, centering lanes, sliding over for joiners, padding parked cars, granting walkers and wheels full adjoining lanes with three bike feet, splitting hazards toward trucks, and sequencing threats singly.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: How should you keep yourself out of other drivers' side and rear blind spots?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Shun blind spots beside and behind others by speeding clear or dropping back, sprint through passing blind zones, and never cruise beside big rigs.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Which six busy pinchpoints demand slower speeds, and where is passing strictly off-limits?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Slow through malls, rush crushes, tight bridges, toll plazas, kid zones and rail crossings, and never pass approaching tracks.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Which three areas must you check before changing lanes, and how many lanes per move?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Change lanes solely past mirror, shoulder and far lane sweeps in quick glances that keep forward watch, shifting exactly one lane per move.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: How many vehicles should you overtake per pass, and what must you scan ahead first?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Pass one car per maneuver after scanning people, narrow bridges and road hazards that could steal the gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How many seconds and feet does a fifty-five-mile-per-hour pass take, and what if unsure?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Fifty five mile per hour passes eat ten seconds and sixteen hundred feet, a third of a mile, against deceptively still oncoming cars, so doubt means wait.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: What mirror cue confirms you have enough room to pull back right after passing?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Reenter only on self found room once both passed headlights fill the rearview, expecting zero courtesy space.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: What time-and-distance window starts a highway pass, and what mirror sight finishes it?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: A highway pass consumes ten seconds and sixteen hundred feet of clear road, then ends only when both victim headlights swim in the mirror.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Why must you skip passing near intersections, rails, or shopping-lot mouths, and are shoulders legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Skip passes at crossings, rails and lot mouths where views die and right turners ignore the lane, and never use any shoulder.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: On highways with fewer than three lanes, when may you legally use the left lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: Reserve left lanes for overtakes, keep right under three lanes except passes, left turns and left exits, and signal each shift.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: Which three maneuvers let drivers leave the right lane on roads under three lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Left lanes exist for overtaking, and roads under three lanes legally pin cruisers right except for passes, left turns and left exits.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: From which lane to which lane must turns travel before any later lane change?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: Turn nearest lane to nearest lane along direct paths that cross minimal traffic and no lines, then shift later only with looks and signals.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: How do right and left turn paths differ, and how do you protect cyclists at corners?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: Swing right turns tight without left feints, cut lefts wide enough for opposing lefts, hold multi turn lanes, and yield turning bikes their rightful road without post pass hooks.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: Why do right turns stay curb-tight while left turns swing a wider arc?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: Right turns hug tight with no left swing feints, while left turns arc wider to gift opposing lefts their own room.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Where is backing banned, how do you fix missed exits, and how do you reverse safely?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: Backing bans travel lanes except parking and K turns, so missed exits mean circling onward, and needed reverses want walk arounds, right shoulder gazes, creeping pace, mirror pauses and spotters.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: Which two maneuvers are the sole legal exceptions to Connecticut's travel-lane backing ban?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Reversing bans all travel lanes outright, with parallel parking and K turns the lone legal exceptions, so missed exits mean looping forward.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: How much forward sight distance do safe passes and hills require, and what do downhills need?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Light up whenever sight dims, demand a third mile or ten seconds of view, treat blind hills like oncoming cars with no close passes, and mirror downhills for runaway heavies.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: How close to a blind hillcrest or curve is passing banned, and how should you picture it?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: Blind hills and bends demand a third mile of sight and ban passes within a third mile, treating hidden crests as phantom oncoming cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Which five road users often cannot see your car and need extra space?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Expect the unseen: blocked corner drivers, blind backers, frosted windshields, umbrella walkers and parked car leapers all deserve extra berth.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: Why must drivers never read maps rolling, wear dual headphones, or rubberneck crash scenes?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.memory_hook: Park maps, bare ears, no gawking
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Never map read rolling, never plug both ears, and never rubberneck crashes, since each steals eyes from braking traffic and breeds new wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: What conditions do posted speed limits assume, and what happens legally on wet, blind, or crowded roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Limits match road design, vehicle kinds and hidden driveways for perfect weather, so wet, blind or crowded miles demand slower wheels and can ticket even posted speeds.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Why must you check your speedometer instead of relying on how fast the car feels, especially leaving an expressway?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Trust speedometers over gut feel, since drivers chronically undersense pace, worst dropping from expressways to local streets.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: How does driving far below normal pace affect trailing traffic, and what should a slow driver do?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: Crawling packs followers and forces risky passes, so pull aside for tailing queues or pick slower roads and quicker pace.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How can both driving the posted speed in a storm and crawling far below traffic get a driver in trouble?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: Posted numbers promise perfect weather only, so storms and crowds can ticket posted speeds, while crawling packs traffic and rightly yields aside.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: When you double speed from thirty to sixty miles per hour, how much does stopping distance grow?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Stopping from sixty needs not double but triple plus the thirty mile per hour distance, so pace must fit sight and surface.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: On dry pavement, how many total reaction-plus-braking feet and city blocks do fifty and thirty miles per hour take?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.memory_hook: Four hundred fifty, two hundred thirty
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Dry fifty costs four hundred reaction plus braking feet, a full block, and thirty costs two hundred, half a block, so shorter sight bans those speeds.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How do stopping physics from doubling speed pair with the four-hundred and two-hundred-foot sight rules?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Doubled speed more than triples stopping need, and sight caps speeds outright: four hundred feet for fifty, two hundred for thirty.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What crashes do panic stops invite, and what habits keep you from needing one?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Panic stops betray blind eyes, invite skids and rear enders, so forecast trouble early, ease or sidestep, and halt fully at every sign and line.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Does Connecticut law ever grant someone the right of way, and what duty always remains?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Law names who yields but grants no one passage, and every driver must still dodge people and cars at all costs.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Who overrides an active traffic light, and who holds priority in crosswalks and bike-path crossings?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Officer waves beat traffic lights, walkers in painted or implied crossings always win passage, and bike path crossings favor riders and walkers.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: What priority do pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog hold, and how must you treat your horn?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Cane and guide dog travelers hold absolute passage, and horns stay silent lest blasts confuse or scare them.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: Who outranks electric traffic signals, and which travelers outrank everyone with horns kept silent?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.memory_hook: Officers top lights, canes top all
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Officer hands outrank electric signals, and cane or dog walkers outrank everyone while forbidding horn noise near them.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: What yield rules govern driveways or shoulders, blocked intersections, overtaking cars, and signaling transit buses?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.memory_hook: Side entries yield, let buses merge
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Driveways, alleys and shoulders yield to main roads, boxes forbid entry without clear exits, passers yield even to slowing leaders, and signaling buses win merges.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Whom must left-turning drivers yield to, and whom must drivers entering a traffic circle yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.memory_hook: Left yields oncoming, entry yields circle
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Left turners bow to straight oncoming traffic, and circle joiners bow to everyone already wheeling inside.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: Who goes first at an unsigned intersection versus at a four-way stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Unsigned corners yield to the right, and four way stops serve first arrivals first with right side ties.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Whom must left turners, rotary entrants, and drivers at unsigned corners each yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Lefts bow to straight oncoming flow, circle mouths bow to inside wheels, and open corners bow to arrivals from the right.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How does the right-hand rule at an all-way stop differ from the right-hand rule at a signless corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.memory_hook: Arrival rules stops, right breaks ties
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: All way stops rank arrival order first and right sides only on ties, unlike signless corners where the right always rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Who goes first at a roundabout, how do you pick lanes and signal exits, and what is banned inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.memory_hook: Yield entering, signal right, never stop
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Roundabouts serve circulating traffic and crosswalk walkers first, guide multi lane entries by signs, exit on right signals past clear gaps, and never halt inside for joiners.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: What three rules govern entering a roundabout gap, signaling out, and keeping moving inside the ring?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.memory_hook: Gap in, right blinker, keep rolling
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Roundabouts yield to inside rings and foot crossings, enter on real gaps signed by lane, exit on right blinks, and never brake inside for joiners.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Where are U-turns completely banned, and what sequence makes a U-turn safe where permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.memory_hook: Never on expressways, signal, stop, scan
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: U-turns need sign checks and shun expressways outright, then run left signal, full stop, traffic scan, and opposite direction right lane entry.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: What must you do when emergency vehicles approach with sirens, air horns, or flashing red or blue lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Sirens, air horns and red or blue flashers order a right edge stop held through passage unless officers or firefighters wave on, clearing intersections first.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: Which lanes must stop for a school bus flashing red lights, who is exempt, and when may you move again?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Flashing red school buses halt all directions and corners except oncoming traffic past medians or barriers, and release only past dark lights with children fully roadside and safety sure.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How does pulling over for an emergency responder differ from stopping for a flashing red school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.memory_hook: Responders right edge, bus stops lanes
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: Flashing responders demand right edge stops held fast, while flashing school buses demand all way stops except oncoming lanes past dividers.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Who always holds the right of way where railroad tracks cross a road?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Trains crossing roads always take the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: Where should you park, how do you secure the vehicle, and which side should you exit from?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.memory_hook: Off lanes, brake, curbside exit, lock
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Park off travel lanes in sight both ways, favor marked bays, brake plus gear or park, exit curbside after door checks, and pocket keys with locked doors.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: Which direction should you turn your front wheels when parking on a hill in Connecticut?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Aim hill parked wheels hard roadside or curbside so runaways roll from traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What extra wheel step distinguishes hill parking from standard flat-ground curb parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Hill wheels crank hard roadside to roll clear of traffic, while flat parking hugs near curbs far from travel lanes with brakes, gears, keys and locks set.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: Which roadway spots, structures, lanes, and clearance zones forbid parking in Connecticut?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.memory_hook: Skip crossings, hydrants, bridges, bike lanes
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Never park in crossings, walks, blocking work zones, within twenty five feet of stop signs or safety zones, ten of hydrants, over a foot from curbs, across driveways or ramps, on bridges or tunnels, wrong sided, in handicap bays unpermitted, doubled, on rails, signed bans, or bike lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: What are Connecticut's exact parking distances for stop signs or safety zones, fire hydrants, and the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.memory_hook: Twenty-five stop, ten hydrant, one curb
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Stop signs and safety zones want twenty five clearing feet, hydrants want ten, and curbs want less than one.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: When must headlights run besides night, what is the wiper rule, and can you drive with parking lights alone?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.memory_hook: Wipers require headlights, never parking lamps
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Burn headlights to be seen, flash highs to announce, always pair wipers with lights by law, light early dusk, shun parking lamps rolling, and glow driving from low suns.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: When should you use high beams, and which traffic or weather conditions require dropping to low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.memory_hook: Empty dark highs, traffic storms low
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Run highs on empty dark stretches for double vision, dim near oncoming blocks, drop low behind cars and crowds, drop low in fog and storms with fog lamps, and never cruise parking lamps alone.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: How should you respond if an oncoming driver leaves high beams on, and what must you never do?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: Answer stuck high beams with quick flashes, then hug the right edge if glare persists, and never duel brights since mutual blindness follows.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: How do empty dark roads, fog or traffic, and stubborn oncoming high beams each set your headlight choice?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.memory_hook: Highs solo, lows crowded, never retaliate
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Empty dark calls high beams, crowds and fog call lows, and stubborn opposing highs earn quick flashes then right edge eyes, never revenge glare.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: How far do high beams reach, what speed does that cap, and what if storms cut sight to two hundred feet?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.memory_hook: Four hundred feet caps near fifty
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: High beams reach four hundred feet capping speed near fifty, soupy storms shrink sight to two hundred feet ordering full pull offs, and blind hills and bends demand stop ready pacing.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: When does a polite light horn tap fit, and when should you sound a sharp warning blast?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.memory_hook: Light tap warns, sharp blast rescues
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Tap horns lightly for lane straying walkers and riders, merging passers and dozing drivers, but blast sharply for darting kids and elders, imminent strikes, and runaway cars.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What type of Connecticut license is Class D, and which vehicles may an unrestricted holder operate?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: A Class D license is the non commercial license, and without restrictions it covers any motor vehicle except a commercial motor vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Which separate Connecticut handbooks cover commercial truck-and-bus drivers versus motorcycle endorsement applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Truck, bus and other commercial or public service drivers use the Commercial Driver License manual, while motorcycle endorsement seekers use the Motorcycle Operator manual.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How does the Class D passenger handbook divide territory from Connecticut's truck-bus and motorcycle manuals?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: This manual and its Class D license cover passenger vehicles only, while truck and bus drivers study the Commercial Driver License manual and riders study the Motorcycle Operator manual.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: Which official Connecticut web address hosts current laws, required document checklists, and knowledge-test booking?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Readers should check ct.gov slash dmv for the latest laws, the required document list, and the online knowledge test appointment.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: What is the leading cause of death for ages fifteen to nineteen, and when does new-driver crash risk peak?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: Crashes are the top killer of fifteen to nineteen year olds, strike mostly in the first two licensed years, and peak in the first six months.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Until what age range is the brain's risk-judgment center still developing—and how does that affect teen drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: The brain region that judges risk keeps maturing into the middle twenties, leaving teens short on hazard judgment.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: How does carrying teen passengers change crash odds, and what role belongs to parents at home?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Teen passenger loads raise crash risk, so families must enforce the state passenger limits at home.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: What two nighttime dangers explain why families and police enforce Connecticut's young-driver curfew?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Night hours bring deadlier crashes and drowsy driving danger for the young, so the state curfew must be enforced.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: How do teen seat-belt habits compare with other ages, despite what buckling up prevents?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Teens wear belts least, yet buckling up is the simplest shield against crash death and grave injury.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: What alcohol standard binds teen drivers, and how much alcohol starts hurting driving skill?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Teens face zero tolerance: a single drink already harms driving skill and crash odds.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which everyday inside-the-cabin distractions lift serious crash risk according to Connecticut's manual?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Calls, passengers, texts, radio tuning, loose pets and like distractions inside the car all lift serious crash risk.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: What credential is mandatory before any behind-the-wheel practice begins—and on every practice drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: No practice driving starts without a learner permit, and the holder carries it on every drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: How old must you be to apply for a Connecticut learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Permit applicants must be at least sixteen years old.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: How does a newly qualified applicant receive their Connecticut photo learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: DMV mails a new photo learner permit to each qualified applicant.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: What health standard applies to permit seekers, and what happens if a risky medical condition exists?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Applicants must meet license holder health and fitness standards, and risky medical conditions need a favorable review before any permit issues.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Which office should an applicant facing possible medical review contact well ahead of applying?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Applicants facing a possible medical review should call the Driver Services Division well ahead at (eight hundred sixty) two hundred sixty-three-five thousand seven hundred twenty.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: How long does a Connecticut learner permit remain valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: A permit lasts until the driver licenses or for two years from issue, whichever ends first.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: Contrast how a fast-moving student's permit ends versus an unhurried learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: A permit ends at licensing or at two years from issue, so an early license beats the calendar and a slow learner faces expiry.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: What consequence can hit a learner who ignores passenger, supervisor, or curfew permit rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Ignoring permit rules can suspend the permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Which two tests must every applicant pass to earn a Connecticut learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: The permit demands passing a vision test plus a twenty five question knowledge test.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: How do you schedule and pay for the knowledge exam, and when does road-test booking unlock?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: Knowledge tests run by appointment with online booking and payment, and the road test books only after the knowledge pass.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: How many questions appear on Connecticut's knowledge test, and how many right answers pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: The knowledge test spans twenty five questions with twenty correct needed to pass, follows this manual, and offers samples on the DMV mobile app.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: Keep Connecticut's two knowledge-test numbers apart: total questions asked versus minimum right answers?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: The knowledge test counts twenty five questions but only twenty correct answers, so the length and the pass mark are two different numbers to keep apart.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Can acing all twenty-five written questions earn a permit if your vision screening falls short?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Vision screening and the knowledge test are separate permit gates: one checks eyesight minimums and the other checks manual knowledge, and both must be passed.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What visual acuity applies across license classes—and what extra field requirement applies with sight in one eye?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Every license class requires vision of at least twenty over forty with or without glasses or contacts; an applicant blind in one eye needs twenty over forty and a visual field of at least one hundred degrees in the other eye.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does Connecticut's vision screening add an extra check for applicants blind in one eye?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Standard applicants meet twenty over forty vision in general, but one eyed applicants must show twenty over forty plus a one hundred degree field in the remaining eye.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What risk do you run at a traffic stop if you drive without corrective lenses listed on your card?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Driving without required corrective lenses risks a citation at a law enforcement stop.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: How often does Connecticut's manual recommend visiting an eye specialist, and why?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Eyes deserve a specialist check every year or two, since weak vision hides without testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: Where must your supervising instructor sit, and what legal responsibility do they share?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: The instructor rides in the front passenger seat, stays alert and ready to take control, and shares responsibility for safe operation with the driver.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Outside formal school lessons, who is the single person a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old permit holder may carry?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Permit holders of sixteen and seventeen take no passengers except a licensed instructor giving lessons plus companions, or one instructing person at least twenty years old, licensed four or more straight years with no suspension in the prior four.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Under what sole training setup may extra student companions ride with a teen permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: The passenger ban lifts during live lessons from a licensed instructor of a commercial school or driver education program.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Which family members—meeting the twenty-plus, four-clean-year rule—may home-train a teen, and who serves as backup?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Home teaching falls to a qualifier of twenty plus with four suspension free licensed years: a parent, foster parent, guardian, grandparent, married minor’s spouse, or failing those an uncle, aunt, sibling, or stepparent.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: When does a qualified twenty-plus family trainer count as the lone legal passenger for a teen permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: A twenty plus adult with four suspension free licensed years may instruct a teen permit holder, but that same adult counts as the single allowed passenger only while actively instructing.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which mandatory course must first-time Connecticut license seekers of every age complete, and where?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: First time license seekers of every age must finish an eight hour Safe Driving Practices class at a Connecticut commercial driving school before licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: Which three driver-training pathways can prepare a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Teen applicants train via a licensed commercial school, a high school program, or home training topped with an eight hour safe driving course holding two parent training hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: What mandatory classroom commitment falls on a teen permit holder's parent or guardian?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: Each teen permit holder’s parent or guardian completes two teaching hours on under eighteen law and teen driving perils inside the required eight hour program.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Which adult or teen applicants must complete the eight-hour Safe Driving Practices course?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Connecticut law requires anyone of any age who has not previously held a Connecticut license or who does not hold a valid out-of-state license to complete an eight-hour Safe Driving Practices course at a Connecticut commercial driving school before obtaining a license.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: How many classroom and road hours make up full school driver-ed, and what certificate unlocks testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: School courses join thirty classroom hours to forty or more coached road hours, ending in form CS-one, the ticket to the road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: Which certificate covers a home-trained teen's eight-hour class, and what topics fill its hours?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.memory_hook: Form c-s-one-a; four alcohol, two parent
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: Home trained drivers also file form CS-1a for an approved eight hour course spending four plus hours on alcohol and drug effects, use dangers, abuse penalties, and the mandatory two hour parent class.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does certificate c-s-one differ in purpose from certificate c-s-one-a?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Form CS-one certifies school course completion for road test eligibility, whereas form CS-1a certifies the home trainer’s eight hour alcohol syllabus course, and the two forms are not interchangeable.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: Which five items does a home teacher formally sign off on the learner permit for road-test day?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.memory_hook: Thirty study, eight-class, manual, forty-road, parent
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: At the road test the home teacher signs off the permit, thirty study hours with the eight hour Safe Driving Practices class, full manual coverage, forty coached road hours, and the two hour parent class.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: If a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old moves to Connecticut already licensed elsewhere, must they still take the eight-hour class?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Out of state licensed teens of sixteen and seventeen must also take the eight hour course for a Connecticut license.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: How many permit days must formal driving-school graduates wait before road-testing versus home-trained applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: School graduates test after one hundred twenty permit days; all other applicants wait one hundred eighty days to the driving exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What exact classroom-and-professional-road hour combination unlocks the shorter one-hundred-twenty-day road-test wait?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: Thirty classroom hours plus eight commercial coached road hours unlock testing at one hundred twenty days; everyone else waits one hundred eighty days past the permit.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: Can pure home training ever qualify for Connecticut's one-hundred-twenty-day road-test waiting period?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: School trained applicants wait one hundred twenty days for the road test while all others wait one hundred eighty days, and the shorter wait belongs only to the school path.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How do total required teen road hours compare with the professional road hours that unlock the one-hundred-twenty-day wait?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: Thirty classroom hours pair with forty coached road hours for school teens, while home teens log thirty study hours plus forty road hours, and neither mix matches the thirty plus eight shortcut to the shorter wait.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Why are brakes uniquely vital, and which four warning signs demand an immediate mechanic visit?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Only the brakes stop the car, so noise, odd smells, a floor bound pedal or pulling aside all send the car to a mechanic.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: How soon must you visit a repair shop if steering feels stiff or responds late?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Steering that fights back or answers late belongs in a mechanic bay before the next drive.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What mechanical problem causes repeated bouncing or wheel-wrestling after hitting bumps?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Repeated bouncing or wrestling the wheel after bumps points at worn shocks and a mechanic visit.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Which exterior lights must work from outside the car, and what headlight flaw needs repair?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Signals, brake, tail and head lights must all work as seen from outside, and a skewed headlight that blinds others needs fixing.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: What four visibility steps prepare your windows, wipers, and windshield before driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Strip snow, ice and frost from every window, keep wipers and washer fluid ready, clean glass inside too, and replace cracked windshields.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What is the sole legitimate purpose of your vehicle's horn?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: The horn serves only as a warning to others, though that warning can save a life.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Where do you find proper tire pressure, and when must you inspect tires for wear?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Worn or bald tires lengthen stopping distance and make wet turns harder, so check tire pressure with a gauge against the owner's manual or driver's door jamb recommendation, and inspect tires for wear and damage monthly and before long road trips.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: How do you run the penny tread check, and what shows safe depth?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: For the penny test, place Lincoln's head into one of the grooves where tread looks lowest: if any part of Lincoln's head is covered by tread, tread depth is safe, whereas lower tread greatly reduces road grip in adverse conditions.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: In the penny tread check, contrast a partly covered Lincoln head against tread below that mark?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: In the penny test, having any part of Lincoln's head covered by tread shows safe tread depth, whereas tread below that mark means road grip in adverse conditions is sharply reduced.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: Which maintenance schedule does every driver owe their vehicle, and why?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Drivers owe their cars the owner manual maintenance schedule, since neglected cars strand and crash their owners.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What five problems can a neglected engine cause, and how do you prevent them?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: A sick engine may fade, stall, drink fuel and foul air, even dying mid road, so keep its manual service dates.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Why are exhaust leaks deadly, and what three habits protect riders from fumes?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: Leaky exhaust can kill riders swiftly, so never idle in a shut garage, crack a window during long idles, and test the system on schedule.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: How many days do you get to repair and retest a vehicle after failing emissions?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: A failed emissions check grants sixty days to repair and retest the vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Which greenhouse gas comes from burning fuel, and how can car shoppers and drivers cut it?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Fuel burning feeds climate change with carbon dioxide, which buyers fight by shopping emissions and economy ratings and by driving thriftily.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: What legal trouble can aftermarket window tint or custom lighting swaps trigger?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Aftermarket tint and lighting swaps can break legal equipment standards.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: What insurance rule governs registered cars, and what sequence follows an unanswered lapse warning?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: Registered cars need unbroken insurance, lapses draw a DMV warning offering a compliance pact and fine, silence suspends the registration, and bare registration bans the road.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: After an insurance lapse, contrast the first warning option with what happens if you ignore it?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: An insurance lapse first buys a warning with a compliance pact and fine, but ignoring that notice kills the registration and grounds the car.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: When do you adjust seat and mirrors, and how do you verify side-mirror aim?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Set seat and mirrors before moving: rearview frames the back glass, side mirrors the flanks, confirmed by leaning forward to glimpse the car side.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Why must you secure loose items and keep cabin floors clear before rolling?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: Stow loose cargo and clear the floors so nothing flies in a stop or wedges beneath the brake pedal.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: Who must buckle up in Connecticut before moving, and why don't airbags replace seat belts?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Connecticut orders belts on every occupant plus proper child restraints before rolling, and airbags never excuse bare belts against side, rear or rollover hits.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: How must two-piece belts and motorized shoulder belts be worn to protect you?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: Two part belts demand both lap and shoulder straps, and auto shoulder belts still need the manual lap buckle against sliding out.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: Which cabin zones do airbags shield, and which crash types still rely on seat belts?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Airbags guard the wheel, dash and windshield only, so belts stay mandatory for side, rear and rollover blows and for holding the driver behind the wheel.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: If both driver and passenger ride unbuckled, how are citations and fines issued?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: An unbelted driver and an unbelted rider each draw their own citation and a seventy five dollar fine.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: Which age group must every driver ensure is buckled, and who gets cited when unbuckled?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: Every driver must see seven to sixteen year old riders belted, every occupant must wear one, and each bare rider earns a citation.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: Do an unbelted driver and passenger split one ticket, or get cited individually?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: Driver and passenger belt tickets land separately: each bare occupant earns a personal citation and fine rather than one shared ticket.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: What restraint rules govern children under age two or thirty pounds versus ages two to five or under forty pounds?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Babies under two or under thirty pounds ride rear facing with a five point harness, and tots of two to five or under forty pounds ride rear or forward facing still harnessed.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Which seats fit kids five to eight or forty to sixty pounds, how do split cases resolve, and what airbag ban applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Kids of five to eight or forty to sixty pounds use a harness or booster, older bigger kids a booster or belt, age weight ties break toward stricter seats, and rear facing seats never face a live front airbag.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: Which age and weight cutoffs separate mandatory rear-facing seats from forward-facing harnessed seats?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Under two years or under thirty pounds means rear facing only, while two to five years or under forty pounds opens the forward facing harnessed seat.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Compare restraint rules for five-to-eight or forty-to-sixty-pound kids versus eight-plus and sixty-plus, including split cases?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: Five to eight years or forty to sixty pounds allows a harness or booster, eight plus years with sixty plus pounds allows a booster or plain belt, and split cases always take the stricter seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: How quickly do seat belts unlatch, how rare are fire or water crashes, and how do belts aid escape?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Belts release in under a second, fire and sinking traps are rare, and a belted rider stays conscious to escape.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: Why does staying belted beat being thrown clear, and which direction do side-struck riders slide?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Staying belted inside beats ejection into traffic, and side struck riders slide toward the impact rather than away.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: Where and at what posted speed limits do most fatal crashes happen?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: More than half of road deaths strike within twenty five miles of home, many on streets posted below forty five miles per hour.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: What real-world impacts match the force of a twenty-five-mile-per-hour head-on crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: A twenty five mile per hour head on hit matches a full speed bicycle into a wall or a three story sidewalk dive, far past bracing.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: Which two twenty-five-unit facts crush the excuse of skipping belts on short local errands?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: Short trip myths die on two numbers: deaths cluster within twenty five miles of home, and a twenty five mile per hour crash hits like a wall or a three story fall.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: When are handheld devices banned, where may drivers call freely, and how do adult and teen rules differ?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Handheld phones and mobile devices stay off on public highways even in traffic stops, parked shoulders allow use, adults may go hands free only, and sixteen and seventeen year olds may use nothing at all.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: Does waiting at a red light lift the phone ban, or must you park safely roadside first?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: A car halted by traffic or signals still counts as operating for the phone ban, while a car parked safely roadside frees the driver to call.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How does hands-free calling legality differ between adult drivers and sixteen- or seventeen-year-olds?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: Adults may talk hands free behind the wheel, but sixteen and seventeen year olds may touch no phone or device whatever, hands free included.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: Which emergency calls may any age driver place, and which on-duty responders may use handhelds?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: In an emergency, a driver of any age may use a cell phone or mobile electronic device to call police or fire departments, an ambulance service, a hospital, a health clinic, a physician's office, or an emergency response operator, while peace officers, firefighters, and ambulance drivers eighteen or older may use handheld devices.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: What three consequences hit an under-eighteen driver convicted of a cell-phone violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: A teen phone ticket counts as a moving violation, convicts under eighteen into a license suspension, and feeds the retraining tally.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Contrast a teen dialing emergency help with a teen making a casual call while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Emergency calls to responders and clinics stay legal at any age, yet a teen social call draws a moving violation, a suspension on conviction, and a retraining mark.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: How does Connecticut define distraction, and how can eyes, hands, or thoughts trigger crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Distraction is anything stealing driving attention, and wandering eyes, hands or thoughts all crash alike, even gazing blindly past seen objects.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: How does mental distraction hide compared with taking eyes off road or hands off wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Eyes off road and hands off wheel show openly, but mind off road hides inside, gazing straight past hazards it never sees.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Who bears legal blame when an inside-the-car distraction causes a collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Drivers own every in-car event outright, so distracted crashes blame the wheel holder, never the distraction.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: Why does crash fault land strictly on the wheel-holder rather than on a cabin distraction?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: The wheel holder owns the whole cabin legally, so crash fault lands on the distracted driver and never on the distraction itself.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which everyday items, screens, passengers, or habits create cabin distractions?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Cabin lures span phones, stereos and climate knobs, GPS, DVD screens, dash panels, grooming, chatty riders, loose kids and pets, meals, maps and dropped grabs.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: Which seven outside-the-window sights lure drivers' eyes away from traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Roadside lures span traffic gawks, police stops, low sun, roadway people and debris, crash scenes, work zones and billboards.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: How do interior cabin traps contrast with exterior roadside traps?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Cabin traps are phones, dials, screens, grooming, riders, meals and maps, while roadside traps are gawk scenes, sun, debris, zones and billboards.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: What pre-drive and cabin habits neutralize distractions before you shift into gear?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: Fight back by tabling fights, eating parked, belting kids with toys, crating pets, presetting dials, ignoring far sights, preplanning maps, shunning car chats and headphones, and expecting surprises.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Which clues reveal a distracted driver nearby, and how much room should you give?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: Spot drifting lanes, yo-yo speeds, fiddling hands, arguing cabins and dawdling rigs, then gift three to four seconds and pass warily past unaware drifters.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does managing your own cabin differ from defending against distracted neighbors?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Self defense presets controls, parks meals and maps, belts and crates the cabin, while other defense reads drifts, surges, fiddles and fights.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Why must you keep three to four seconds back and pass distracted leaders warily?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Distracted leaders earn three to four seconds of room and extra wary passes, since unaware drifters can slide across without warning.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: How does physical or mental fatigue impair a driver much like alcohol or drugs?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: Fatigue means body or mind tiredness that warps vision, judgment, speed sense, decisions and temper like drink or drugs, and can end asleep at speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: Which four driver groups face sharply elevated risk for drowsy-driving crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: Groups at special risk for fatigue-related crashes include sixteen- to twenty-four-year-olds who often need extra sleep, people with untreated obstructive sleep apnea facing seven times the risk of falling asleep at the wheel, night-shift workers facing nearly six times the risk, and rotating-shift or over-sixty-hour-a-week workers who must be especially careful.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: By how much do untreated obstructive sleep apnea and night-shift work multiply wheel-sleep risk?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: People sixteen to twenty-four often need more sleep than average adults, untreated obstructive sleep apnea raises the risk of falling asleep at the wheel seven times, working the night shift raises that risk by nearly six times, and rotating-shift or over-sixty-hour weekly workers must be particularly careful.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: What sleep bank, break interval, passenger help, and medication rule prevent highway fatigue?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: Pre trip right with seven to nine sleep hours, hundred mile or two hour rest breaks, a relief companion, and zero alcohol or drowsy pills.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: Which four preparation pillars protect drivers before starting a long road trip?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: Trip prep banks seven to nine sleep hours with hundred mile or two hour pauses, plus a relief rider and no drowsy pills or drinks.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: What physical and driving warning signs tell you drowsy nodding has begun?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Nod warnings flash as radio cranking and window drops, drooping lids and heads, yawns, lane drifts and missed exits, daydreams, restlessness, dull reactions and fading drive.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: Once yawning, daydreaming, or lane drifting starts, what is the only safe response?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: Body alarms are lid droops, yawns, drifts, missed exits, daydreams and dullness, and their answer is stopping to sleep, never pressing on.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: How do short parked naps, two-cup caffeine timing, and midnight-to-six hours fit fatigue defense?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: Fight nods by stopping to sleep, napping fifteen to twenty parked minutes, sipping two coffee equivalents ahead of naps without trusting caffeine alone, dodging midnight to six driving, and prizing real sleep most.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: How does pairing two coffees with a fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap compare against true sleep?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Short naps of fifteen to twenty minutes pair with two coffee equivalents taken first, yet caffeine fades, midnight to six stays cursed, and only sleep truly restores.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: What pattern marks typical drowsy crashes, and what must you do after hitting rumble strips?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Tired wrecks run solo off roads into rolls or fixed hits, while rumble grooves roar and shake warnings that order instant safe pull offs and alertness checks.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: How do colds, pain, or store-bought and prescription drugs affect driving, and what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: Colds, infections, aches and many counter or prescription drugs all dull driving, so hand keys over when ill and quiz doctors about risky conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How do worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness affect driving, and how do you counter them?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: Worry, thrill, fear, fury and gloom all cloud thinking and tempt risks, so cool off-road, soothe with radio if calm, pad trip time against darting, or cede the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: What actions match hitting rumble strips, feeling sick, taking sedating meds, or feeling upset?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Running over a shoulder rumble strip requires pulling off at a safe place immediately to check alertness; when unwell, let someone else drive; avoid alcohol and sedating medications by checking labels or asking your doctor; and when strong emotions affect driving, cool off off-road, leave extra time, or let someone else drive.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What share of fatal crashes involves alcohol, and why are new drivers hit harder than veterans?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Alcohol rides in over forty percent of fatal crashes, any sip lifts crash odds, and green drivers suffer worse than veterans.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which four financial, legal, and personal losses hit drivers caught driving after drinking?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Drinking drivers risk stiff fines, pricier insurance, lost licenses and jail cells.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: What brain function does alcohol numb first, and why does the manual compare overdrinking to sunburn?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Drink travels stomach to blood to brain, first numbing judgment itself, so overdose announces only past the point of return like late felt sunburn.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Which six core driving abilities deteriorate further as blood alcohol climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Rising doses dull reflexes, sight, alertness, distance and speed math, other car tracking, and basic vehicle control.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: What is Connecticut's safest rule on drinking and driving, especially for drivers under twenty-one?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Safest counsel is never drive after drinking, since any dose can impair and arrest, and under twenty one a single drink may suffice.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Which three standard pours equal one drink, and why are exotic mixed drinks tricky?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: One drink means a shot and a half of eighty proof liquor, a regular twelve ounce beer, or a five ounce wine, while exotic mixes can pack several.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How do liquor, regular beer, and wine servings match up against fancy mixed cocktails?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A shot and a half of liquor, a regular beer, or a five ounce wine each count one drink, while fancy mixed drinks can secretly equal several.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Why do coffee, cold showers, exercise, and fresh air fail, and what sobers you?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Coffee, air, exercise and cold showers never hurry sobriety; only passing time does.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: What is the sole factor that clears alcohol from your bloodstream?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Coffee, fresh air, workouts and cold showers never speed sobriety; only elapsed time clears alcohol from the body.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What two smart transport plans bring everyone home safely from parties with alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Party smart by rotating a dry designated driver among two plus friends, or by riding transit and cabs home.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Which four common prescription or over-the-counter medicines can impair driving like alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Headache, cold, allergy and nerve pills, prescription or store bought, can sedate and warp reflexes, judgment, vision and alertness like liquor or worse.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: What must you check before driving on medication, and why never combine pills with alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Read every drug label for driving warnings, quiz doctors or druggists when unsure, and never mix pills with alcohol lest effects multiply toward sickness or death.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: How do cold, headache, allergy, or nerve drugs act solo versus combined with alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Cold, headache, allergy and nerve medicines alone mimic liquor behind the wheel, and stacked with liquor they multiply toward grave illness or death.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: Which three chemical samples can officers require, and what minimum suspension and interlock follow failure?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Drunk driving draws court plus Commissioner penalties: a blood, breath or urine test, then on failure at least forty five suspended days plus an ignition interlock for six months minimum, longer with priors.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What minimum suspension and ignition-interlock term hit a driver of any age who refuses chemical sampling?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Refusing every test at any age still costs forty five days plus a year minimum interlock, stretching with priors.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How does minimum ignition-interlock time compare between failing a chemical sample and refusing one?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Failing the chemical test costs forty five days plus six interlock months, while refusing every test costs forty five days plus a full interlock year.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: What blood-alcohol threshold, locations, and penalties govern Connecticut's under-twenty-one zero-tolerance law?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Under twenty one zero tolerance treats any measurable drink, two hundredths percent and up on roads or private land, as arrestable, with failure costing forty five days and a year minimum interlock.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Where does Connecticut enforce its two-hundredths-percent underage limit, and what penalty follows?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Drivers under twenty one face zero tolerance at two hundredths percent on public roads and private lots alike, with failures drawing forty five days and a year minimum interlock.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Which five conviction categories suspend sixteen- and seventeen-year-old driving privileges in Connecticut?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Teen convictions for restriction breaks, speeding, reckless driving, street racing or phone use all suspend sixteen and seventeen year old licenses or licensing privileges.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What suspension terms and restoration fee hit first versus repeat teen restriction violations?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: First restriction breaks cost thirty days plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines, while later ones cost six months or until eighteen, whichever lasts longer, plus the same money.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How does Connecticut measure the suspension length for a repeat teen restriction violation?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Repeat restriction breaks span six months or stretch to the eighteenth birthday, whichever lasts longer, on top of the per offense ladders.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: How long are the first, second, and third teen cell-phone or texting suspensions, plus restoration fee?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Teen phone and texting tickets ladder thirty days, then ninety, then six months, each plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: What suspension ladder and restoration fee hit teens convicted of speeding twenty or more over?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Teen speeding twenty plus over ladders sixty days, then ninety, then six months, each plus a hundred seventy five dollar restoration fee and court fines.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How does the opening teen phone suspension compare with twenty-over teen speeding across three strikes?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Teen phone tickets climb thirty, ninety, then one hundred eighty days, while teen twenty over speeding climbs sixty, ninety, then one hundred eighty days.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What suspension and jail exposure hit teens on first versus repeat GDL or reckless counts?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: Teen GDL and reckless counts open six months plus fees and fines or up to thirty jail days, then year long suspensions with fines or up to a year locked, second and third times alike.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What suspension and jail exposure apply to first and repeat teen street-racing convictions?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Teen street racing opens six months plus fees and fines or up to a year locked, then year long suspensions with the same money or jail, second and third times alike.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How does maximum first-offense jail time compare between teen reckless counts and street racing?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: First GDL and reckless counts add up to thirty jail days, but first street racing counts add up to a full jail year.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Which three severe charges bar drivers under eighteen from youthful-offender status?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Someone under eighteen cannot be considered a youthful offender for negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading responsibility after a crash resulting in death or serious injury, or driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: Which five youthful-offender findings still get reported to DMV for license suspension?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: Youthful findings for reckless, suspended or property flight driving, street racing and officer eluding still reach DMV for license suspensions.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How do Connecticut's three youthful-offender bars contrast with its five DMV-disclosed youth adjudications?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Under eighteen, negligent homicide with a motor vehicle, evading a crash causing death or serious injury, and DUI of alcohol or drugs bar youthful offender status, whereas youthful offender adjudications for reckless driving, driving under suspension, evading a property-damage or non-serious-injury crash, street racing, or eluding police are disclosed to DMV for suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: How must you park and behave inside your car during a Connecticut police stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Blue flashing or wailing stops want a right edge park clear of crossings, frozen cabin movement, wheel and visible hands, papers on request only, shut doors, seated waiting and lit domes by night.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Where is the proper venue to contest a traffic citation you believe is unfair?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Contested tickets get fought in court, never argued roadside with the officer.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: How many moving or suspension convictions trigger operator retraining at twenty-four-and-under versus twenty-five-plus?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: Retraining school teaching operation basics, attitude versus aggression, and safe habits awaits drivers twenty four and under after two moving or suspension counts and older drivers after three.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: Which three teen violations trigger retraining, including what rule on hands-free phones under eighteen?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: Teen retraining triggers include permit breaches, GDL breaches, and any under eighteen phone touching even hands free.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What penalty hits if a retrained driver picks up another moving violation within three years?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: One more moving count within three retrained years suspends the license at least thirty days.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: How do Connecticut's age-based retraining thresholds combine with the three-year post-course rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Drivers age twenty-four or younger with two or more moving or suspension violations, and drivers age twenty-five or older with three or more such convictions, must complete certified operator retraining, and another moving violation within three years of completion brings a suspension of at least thirty days.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Why should you signal every turn or lane change even when the street looks completely empty?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.memory_hook: Signal every move, unseen eyes watch
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: Build the habit of signaling each direction change, even on empty roads, since a hidden traveler may need your warning.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: How many seconds ahead must you start signaling, and why wait until passing intervening driveways or side streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.memory_hook: At least three seconds, pass driveways
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Start the signal at least three seconds before moving, yet hold it until past any streets or driveways short of your turn, like a driveway just past a crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: When another car waits to pull out between you and your upcoming turn, when should you flick your signal on?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: When a car is about to enter between you and your turn, signal only after passing it, or it may pull into your path.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How do Connecticut's three-second minimum warning and the rule on nearby driveways work together?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.memory_hook: Three seconds minimum, clear earlier drives
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Three seconds of warning is the floor, yet a blinker fired before the driveways and crossings ahead lies to entering drivers, so count down early but commit late.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Why must you check your dashboard blinker indicator after finishing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: After finishing a turn or lane change, check the signal is off, since gentle turns may not cancel it and a stray blink invites wrong guesses.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: What false message does an uncancelled turn signal send after a soft lane change or curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: A forgotten blinker after a soft turn reads as a second turn coming, unlike a deliberate hold through the maneuver, so eyes must confirm the cancel each time.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How many times should you tap the brake pedal before an unexpected slowdown, and what spots call for it?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.memory_hook: Tap brakes three or four times
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Slow as early as safe, and where a stop will surprise followers, tap the brake pedal three or four times: exits without lanes, parking or turning ahead of a crossing, expected turns, or hidden road hazards.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How should brake-light warnings differ between a routine slowdown and a surprise stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.memory_hook: Steady for expected, taps for surprise
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Routine slowdowns speak through steady brake lamps, while surprise halts demand three or four quick taps, and mixing the two leaves followers guessing.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: If mechanical trouble strikes, what steps come first, and where must you avoid stopping if stuck on the roadway?
