sec10-card-sec10-F06.memory_hook: Pull off, flashers, keep long sightlines
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: When trouble strikes, pull clear of traffic if possible, switch flashers on, alert authorities, and if stuck on the road, halt where sight lines are long, never just past a hill or curve.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: How do you warn traffic behind a stalled car with or without flares, and what lane mistake is forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.memory_hook: Flares behind, white cloth, off lane
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: Set flares behind a stalled car so lanes can shift; without flares, wave traffic by from a safe shoulder with a white cloth, raise the hood or tie cloth to the antenna, mirror or handle, and never stand or change tires in a lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: What sequence can stop your car safely if the service brakes suddenly fail?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.memory_hook: Pump pedal, ease parking brake, downshift
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: With dead brakes, pump the pedal hard, then ease the parking brake on slowly without locking the rear wheels, releasing at any skid, and if still rolling, drop gears and coast to a safe off-road stop, never driving on.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: How should your hands and feet respond when a tire suddenly blows out or goes flat?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.memory_hook: Grip tight, lift gas, light brake
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: On a sudden flat, grip the wheel tight, hold straight, lift off the gas, brake lightly, and roll to a safe shoulder instead of halting in the road.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How does your brake-pedal action during brake failure contrast with your brake-pedal action during a tire blowout?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.memory_hook: Pump dead brakes, spare blown tires
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: When brakes fail, pump repeatedly; if that fails, ease on the parking brake without locking rear wheels, then downshift if needed and stop off-road. For a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, keep straight, release the accelerator, brake lightly and pull off safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What happens to steering and braking if your engine dies while moving, and how do you pull off?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.memory_hook: Heavy wheel, press brake very hard
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: If the engine quits moving, keep a firm grip though steering turns heavy, steer off the road, and press the brake pedal very hard to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What steps should you take if your headlights suddenly go dark at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.memory_hook: Slow gently, pull off, flick switch
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: When headlights die, slow gently, leave the road fast, flick the switch a few tries, then run flashers, signals or fog lamps, and do not keep driving.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: What is the safest sequence if your engine suddenly races on its own with a stuck accelerator?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.memory_hook: Eyes forward, shift neutral, pull off
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: If the motor races on its own, eyes forward, shift quickly to neutral, pull off when clear, and kill the engine.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Why must you never turn the ignition key to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Never twist the ignition to lock while rolling, or the wheel freezes and control is gone.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What three collision-avoidance actions can dodge or soften almost any impending crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: A crash can almost always be dodged or softened, with three answers to pick from: stop, turn, or speed up.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: In what crash scenario is pressing the gas pedal your smartest escape, and what comes right after?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.memory_hook: Side or rear threat, open ahead
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Sometimes the escape is forward gas, when a side or rear strike looms and open road waits ahead; ease off once past the danger.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: Among the three collision-avoidance options, what exact combination of threat direction and road space calls for speeding up?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.memory_hook: Rear or side threat, clear front
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: To avoid a collision, drivers have three options—stop, turn, or speed up—and speeding up may be best or necessary when another vehicle is about to hit from the side or behind and there is room ahead to escape danger, slowing down once danger passes.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: How must you use the brake pedal during an emergency stop in a vehicle with antilock brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: With antilock brakes, push the pedal down as hard as you can and hold through any pushback, since easing off kills the system.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: How do you make the fastest emergency stop in a car without antilock brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.memory_hook: Squeeze hard, lift at skid, repeat
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Without antilock brakes, brake hard short of locking, and at the first skid, lift fast, then press again, repeating until halted.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: How does emergency hard-stop footwork differ between antilock brakes and conventional non-ABS brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.memory_hook: Pin ABS down, modulate plain brakes
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Antilock pedals beg to be pinned through their shudder, while plain brakes punish the same stomp with a skid that only a quick lift and re-press can cure.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Why can steering beat braking at highway speed, how do you hold the wheel, and what does ABS allow?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.memory_hook: Turns quicker, both hands, ABS steers
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: A car usually turns sooner than it stops, so grip with both hands, aim where you want to go, hold control after the swerve to dodge a second crash, and with antilock brakes you may brake and turn together.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: Without antilock brakes, how do you combine braking and steering, and why choose off-road over oncoming lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Without antilock brakes, brake first, release, then turn, loading the front tires for a tighter arc without locking them or cutting so sharp the car plows ahead; leaving the road beats meeting another car head-on.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What separates steering during an emergency stop with antilock brakes versus without them?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.memory_hook: ABS steers braking, plain releases first
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: With antilock help the wheel may turn mid-braking, but without it the driver must brake, release, then steer, since locked fronts only plow straight.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: What triggers a tire skid, and why is preventing one far better than trying to recover?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Skids strike when tires outrun their grip, on wet or icy roads or simply too fast for the bend, and a sliding car answers no command, so prevention wins.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: If your car starts skidding, what should you do with the brake and steering wheel until straight?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.memory_hook: Stay off brake, steer target, unwind
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: In a skid, stay off the brake until speed bleeds down, steer toward your target, unwind the wheel as the car straightens to block a swing the other way, and keep correcting left and right until it tracks true.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: Why must your feet lift off the pedals while your hands steer and counter-steer in a skid?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: A sliding car ignores the brake and slides further for it, so feet lift while hands steer and counter-steer, the reverse of every dry-road instinct.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: What restraint protects occupants best in any crash, and what emergency gear belongs in the vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Belts come first against crash injury, lap plus shoulder every seat, and a stocked kit of flares, first aid and basic tools rides along for the aftermath.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: How should you position your body, head, and foot right before being struck from behind?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.memory_hook: Press back, headrest, stand on brakes
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Braced for a rear strike, pin yourself to the seatback, rest your head on the restraint, and stand on the brakes so the shove cannot launch you onward.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Why do seat belts matter critically in a side-impact collision where front airbags cannot help?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: A side slam flings you toward the blow, where front airbags give no aid, so belts must hold you at the wheel while you steer or brake against the next impact.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: If a frontal collision cannot be avoided, why aim for a glancing blow and rely on your belts after the airbag?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.memory_hook: Angle glancing blow, belts guard second
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Meeting a frontal crash, twist for a glancing blow over a square hit, ride out the airbag’s burst and fall, and let the belts pin you for a possible second strike.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: How do survival actions differ across rear, side, and unavoidable frontal impacts?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.memory_hook: Rear brakes, side belts, front glance
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: Rear blows pin you back with brakes set, side blows lean on belts alone past useless front bags, and frontal blows beg a twist toward the glance — one brace never fits all three.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: When should you stop at someone else's crash, and why must uninvolved drivers never slow to stare?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Pass others’ crashes by unless you are part of them or no help has come, and never detour to stare, since rubberneckers choke the path of police, fire, ambulance and tow crews.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What legal duties bind any driver involved in a collision, including hitting a parked car or injury crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.memory_hook: Stop immediately, locate owner, call police
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Join a crash and you must halt, hunt down a parked car’s owner, call police for any injury or death, and know that slipping away before officers finish is a crime.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: What five steps prevent fires, electrocution, and secondary crashes at a collision scene?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.memory_hook: Clear lanes, ignitions off, set flares
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: At the scene, park at its edge and clear of lanes, kill every wreck’s ignition, smoke nothing near spilled fuel, shun fallen wires, and flare the road so traffic skirts the wreckage.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: How should you prioritize and treat injured crash victims while waiting for medics?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.memory_hook: Do not move, breathing, bleeding, warmth
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: For the hurt, summon police and medics, naming any fire, move nobody unless flames or traffic threaten, aid the silent ones first checking breath then blood, press wounds hard with hand or cloth, give no drink even water, and wrap the shocked in coats against the chill.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: What details must you exchange after a crash, how do you handle an unfound parked-car owner, and when must police be notified?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.memory_hook: Swap full details, note, report damage
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Trade names, addresses, license numbers, plate, make, model, year and insurance details with all drivers and witnesses, log the damage, answer officers fully, pin a dated note with your contact on an unfound parked car, and always file with police when hurt, killed or property breaks.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: At a collision, when may victims be moved, when must you stop, and when must officers be called?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.memory_hook: Always stop, rarely move, report harm
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: The injured stay put unless fire or traffic hunts them, and the crash itself always halts you, though officers need calling only for hurt, killed or broken property.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What five lane-control tasks do pavement markings handle along the street?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.memory_hook: Splits lanes, guides turns, marks stops
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Paint on the road splits lanes, sets passing and lane-change permission, points turn lanes, marks stop lines and carves walkways, together steering lane control.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which roadway edges do solid white edge lines and solid yellow edge lines each mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Edge lines trace the road rim, solid white guarding the right shoulder and solid yellow the left rim of divided streets.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What color separates lanes moving the same direction, and how do dashed white and solid white differ?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Same-way lanes part on white, dashed white inviting a safe lane change and solid white ordering drivers to hold their lane short of special cause.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: How can you tell traffic direction immediately just from whether a lane divider is white or yellow?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: White paint always parts travelers bound the same way, while any yellow center line always splits opposing streams, so color alone names the traffic bargain.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Between two same-direction lanes, what changes for lane changers when dashed white becomes solid white?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: Dashed white waves lane changers across when clear, but solid white locks them in their lane short of special cause, one dash deciding freedom.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What do yellow center lines divide, when does a dashed yellow line allow passing, and what do yield lines mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.memory_hook: Opposing lanes, dashed passes, yield pauses
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Yellow centers split opposing flows, dashed yellow pairing single opposing lanes where passing stands open, while yield lines flag must-yield ground such as mid-block crossings.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: When a dashed yellow stripe runs alongside a solid yellow stripe, which direction is allowed to pass?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Where dashed yellow runs beside solid, only the broken side may pass, the solid side stays put.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: What is the only legal reason to cross twin solid yellow center stripes on a two-way road?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Twin solid yellow stripes crown the middle of two-way roads, crossed solely to swing left into or out of alleys, private roads, driveways and streets.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: Between a lone dashed yellow center line and solid yellow center lines, what grants permission to pass?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: A lone dashed yellow middle invites passing between single opposing lanes, while solid yellow middles forbid it except for left turns to local doors, so the dash, not the color, grants passage.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How does a mixed solid-and-dashed yellow center pair differ from double solid yellow stripes?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.memory_hook: Mixed lets one pass, double neither
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Mixed yellow centers split permission by side, broken-side drivers passing while solid-side drivers hold, unlike twin solid stripes that bind both sides to left-turn crossings only.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Where must you halt for a required stop, whom must you yield to at crosswalks, and why watch unpainted corners?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.memory_hook: Stop before line, watch unmarked corners
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: When a sign or signal requires a stop, you must stop before reaching the stop line, yield to pedestrians in or about to enter a crosswalk, and stay alert for pedestrians at intersections because not all crosswalks are marked.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How do stop lines and crosswalks work together at intersections, including corners with no crosswalk paint?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.memory_hook: Stop behind bar, yield all crosswalks
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Stop lines mark where your vehicle must stop before reaching the line for a sign or signal, while crosswalks define where pedestrians cross and require yielding to pedestrians in or about to enter them, including unmarked crosswalks at intersections.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: How are restricted lanes marked, and who qualifies for transit, bicycle, and HOV diamond lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.memory_hook: Signs and diamonds reserve special users
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: Reserved lanes announce themselves by signs and white diamonds, transit or bus for buses alone, bicycle for bikes alone, and diamond HOV lanes for cars meeting the posted rider count.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What do diagonal stripes, hazard funnel lines, double solid white, painted curbs, and sharrow bike chevrons each indicate?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.memory_hook: Stripes block, white locks, sharrows share
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: Odd paint warns too: diagonal stripes cage fixed blocks, solid lines funnel past hazards, twin solid white bars any lane swap, curbs and fire lanes may ban parking by local order, and a sharrow’s chevrons over a bike mark a shared lane to watch for riders.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How does a lane painted with a white diamond differ from a lane painted with a bicycle sharrow?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Diamond lanes exclude all but their named riders, buses, bikes, or counted carpools, while a sharrow’s chevrons merely warn that bikes may share an open lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: What maneuvers use a shared middle lane, what paint borders it, and how can rush hour change it?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.memory_hook: Both ways turn left, check rush
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Shared middle lanes serve left turns both ways, U-turns where lawful, under alternating turn arrows between solid and dashed yellow walls, sometimes flipping reversible at rush, so enter only when the way reads safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: What pavement lines edge a reversible lane, and what do green arrow, red X, blinking yellow X, and steady yellow X mean?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Reversible lanes swap direction by hour inside double-dashed yellow, so read the signs and lamps first: green arrow ride it, red X shun it, blinking yellow X turns only, steady yellow X clear out soon.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: How does a shared center left-turn lane differ in purpose and flow from a reversible travel lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.memory_hook: Shared serves turns, reversible flips flow
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: Shared center lanes are reserved for left turns and permitted U-turns by traffic from both directions—though some become reversible lanes during rush hours—whereas reversible lanes carry traffic one way at certain times and the opposite way at other times under lane-control signs and lights.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: What does each traffic-signal color mean, and in what bottom-to-top order are vertical lamps usually stacked?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.memory_hook: Green bottom, yellow middle, red top
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: Signal heads speak stop and go, green for go-when-safe, yellow for caution, red for halt, usually stacked green, yellow, red from the ground up, though lone single-color lamps guard some spots.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: What does a steady red light command, and what four checks are required before turning right on red?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.memory_hook: Full stop first, clear before right
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Red commands a full stop until green returns with the crossing empty, though right turns may roll after halting, scanning oncoming traffic, honoring any no-turn sign and sparing the walkers ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What does a steady yellow light warn of, and what should you do if already inside the intersection when it turns yellow?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.memory_hook: Brake when safe, clear if inside
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Yellow warns red is next, so brake when safe, but a car already inside the crossing when yellow dawns must roll on through.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Even when your light turns green, which four groups or situations must you still yield to?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.memory_hook: Green still yields to clear conflicts
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Green opens the crossing with duties attached: bow to emergency rigs and legal rivals, drain waiting cross traffic first, turn left only through a safe gap and yield right turns to crossing feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: How do you obey a blinking red signal versus a blinking yellow signal?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: A blinking red light equals a stop sign, halting fully before a safe entry, while blinking yellow just begs slower, warier rolling.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How do steady red and yellow signals differ in strictness from blinking red and blinking yellow signals?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Steady lamps command absolutely, red halting and yellow warning of red, while blinking red softens to stop-sign duty and blinking yellow to mere caution.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: What does a red arrow, a yellow arrow, and a green arrow each tell drivers in that turn lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.memory_hook: Red bars, yellow ends, green protects
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Arrows aim the order: red arrow bars its heading until green arrow or lamp frees it, yellow arrow ends green-arrow shelter and counsels stopping, green arrow blesses the turn with cross and opposing lanes held.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: Which signal arrow guarantees a protected turn, and how do red and yellow arrows restrict that movement?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.memory_hook: Green protects, yellow closes, red blocks
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Red arrows jail one heading until green frees it, yellow arrows warn the green shelter is collapsing, and green arrows alone promise a defended turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: What lamp layout identifies a HAWK beacon, how does it activate, and what is its purpose?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: The HAWK beacon, a yellow eye beneath twin reds, wakes by walker button and freezes cars to a full stop until the crossing empties.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Walk through all five HAWK beacon phases from dark through blinking yellow, solid yellow, solid red, and blinking red?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.memory_hook: Dark rolls, yellows warn, reds stop
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Read the HAWK phases: dark means roll on, blinking yellow means a walker woke it, solid yellow means red approaches, solid red means feet in the street so stop, blinking red means stop then creep once the walkers clear as it sleeps.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: At a HAWK crosswalk signal, how does solid red differ from flashing red once you stop?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.memory_hook: Solid holds, flashing goes when clear
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: At a HAWK signal, solid red means pedestrians are in the crosswalk and motorists must stop, whereas flashing red means the signal is about to deactivate and drivers must stop but may proceed once pedestrians have cleared the crosswalk.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: What five types of information do road signs deliver, and how can you preview a sign before reading its text?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Road signs preach rules, hazards, position, routes and services, and their silhouettes and hues preview the message inside.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: What action does a downward-pointing triangle command, and what does a diamond-shaped sign warn about?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Downward triangles order yielding at a sane pace with a halt if needed, while diamonds cry hazard ahead and beg caution with brakes at the ready.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: What does an eight-sided red sign command, where do you halt, and whom must you yield to afterward?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.memory_hook: Eight sides halt, yield both ways
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Eight-sided red always halts, demanding a full stop at the sign, line, crosswalk or curb, then deference to every crosser from both sides.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How do a diamond, a downward triangle, and an octagon rank from caution up to mandatory halt?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.memory_hook: Diamond cautions, triangle yields, octagon halts
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Triangles throttle and sometimes halt for others, diamonds only preach caution for hazards, and octagons freeze every wheel outright, three shapes in rising strictness.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: How do tall vertical rectangles differ from wide horizontal ones, and what does a five-sided pentagon mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.memory_hook: Tall states law, pentagon marks school
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Rectangles and squares carry orders, cautions and guidance, tall ones speaking law and wide ones pointing the way, while five-sided shields fence school ground and student crossings, their arrow plaques pinning the walk.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Which lone sign outline marks school zones, and how does rectangle orientation separate law from guidance?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.memory_hook: Vertical rules, horizontal guides, pentagon schools
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Tall rectangles legislate while wide ones inform, and five-sided shields alone fence school ground, so posture plus corners name the duty.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What hazard do round signs announce ahead, and what does a triangular pennant on the left side of a two-lane road mark?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.memory_hook: Round warns rails, pennant bans passing
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Round signs foretell rails ahead and beg slower eyes and ears, and three-cornered pennants on the left rim of two-way two-lane roads open a marked no-passing stretch.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: How does the warning on a circular sign differ from the rule marked by a left-side pennant?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.memory_hook: Circle previews tracks, pennant starts ban
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Round boards foresee rails and summon eyes and ears, while left-rim pennants merely open a painted no-passing stretch.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: What messages belong to red, black-and-white, yellow, and orange road signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.memory_hook: Red forbids, white rules, orange works
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Red signs always command obedience, from halts and yields to wrong-way bans, black and white ones either command or mark routes, yellow warns of road dangers and orange warns of work-zone dangers.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How do red, black-and-white, yellow, and orange divide into two rule colors and two warning colors?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Red always orders, black-and-white either orders or routes, plain yellow warns of the road and orange warns of its builders, four hues in two pairs.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: What do green, fluorescent yellow-green, blue, and brown signs each guide or protect?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.memory_hook: Green routes, yellow-green schools, blue services
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Green guides to places, roads and distances, glowing yellow-green guards walkers, riders and pupils, blue guides to roadside services and brown to parks and playgrounds.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How do green, glowing yellow-green, blue, and brown split navigation, vulnerable road users, services, and recreation?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Green points to places and miles, glowing yellow-green shields the vulnerable, blue sells roadside comfort and brown courts the outdoors, guide hues split by errand.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What colors and shapes carry regulatory rule signs, what rules do they set, and what symbol bans a move?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.memory_hook: Red circle slash brands forbidden moves
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Rule signs stand square, tall or special-cut in white, red or black, scripting direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and odd cases, with a red ring and slash branding the banned move.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: How do the red octagon with white letters and the red-and-white downward triangle differ in action?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: The eight-sided red stop board with pale letters freezes every wheel until crossers clear, and the red-and-white downward triangle throttles speed and surrenders passage to the busier road.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: Where do red-ball white-bar Do Not Enter signs stand, and what must you do if you face Wrong Way signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: A white bar floating in a red ball bars every entry at ramps, crossovers and one-way mouths, and wrong-way boards mark the forbidden side of one-way streets and split highways, ordering a turnaround short of them.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: How do Stop, Yield, Do Not Enter, and Wrong Way signs compare in what each red board refuses?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Octagon red demands the dead stop, triangle red-white only bends to busier wheels, the barred red ball locks whole entries and wrong-way boards punish the reversed, four reds of climbing refusal.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: Where are No U-Turn signs typically posted, and how are lane-specific turn bans displayed?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.memory_hook: Highways ban U-turns, poles ban turns
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: No-U-turn boards guard split highways and fast roads, while movement-ban boards veto lane or approach turns from poles or gantries, sometimes echoed by painted arrows.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What rules do One-Way signs, lane-use control signs, and Keep Right divider signs each enforce?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.memory_hook: Follow one-way, lane arrows, pass right
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: One-way boards chain drivers to the arrow’s heading, lane-use boards bless each lane’s allowed move, and keep-right boards steer wheels past islands, medians and mid-road blocks to the shown side.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How does restriction scope differ across No U-Turn, turn-ban, One-Way, and Keep Right signs?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: No-U-turn boards spare only the reversal, movement bans veto named lane turns, one-way boards jail the whole heading, and keep-right boards merely dodge mid-road blocks.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What hidden hazards trigger No Passing Zone signs, and when may you use a reopened passing stretch?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.memory_hook: Short sightlines ban, pass when safe
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: No-passing boards map sight-short ground where hills, bends, crossings and driveways hide entering cars, joining paint to open and close passing stretches that may be used only when safe.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Who may park in wheelchair-symbol spaces, and what ceiling do speed limit signs set?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.memory_hook: Authorized disabled permits, maximum lawful pace
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Wheelchair-marked stalls belong to drivers holding disabled privileges alone, and speed boards post the fastest lawful pace for the stretch.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What shape and colors mark standard warning signs, and what do Signal Ahead and Lane Ends signs announce?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Caution boards usually wear yellow with black ink in diamond cut, preaching slower wheels and ready brakes, with signal-ahead and lane-shrink variants heralding lights and merging funnels.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What do pedestrian signs with arrow plaques, flashing crosswalk beacons, and Two-Way Traffic signs each warn of?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.memory_hook: Pinpoint crosswalks, active beacons, divider ending
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Walker-crossing boards with arrow plaques pin the footpath, flashing beacons guard busy unsignaled crossings, and two-way boards warn the divider is ending.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: How should you respond to School warning signs, Slippery When Wet signs, and Stop Ahead signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.memory_hook: Slow near schools, widen wet gaps
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: School boards slow wheels near grounds and guards, slick-when-wet boards stretch following gaps and soften braking and swerving, and stop-ahead boards preview the octagon.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What do No Passing Zone pennants forbid, how do Merge warnings work, and what do small plaques under warnings post?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.memory_hook: No overtaking, cooperative merge, safe speed
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Zone-start boards ban passing the cars ahead, merge boards fuse two lanes into one by mutual grace, and small plaques beneath cautions whisper the safe speed for the hazard.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Which warning signs preview forced stops, which manage merging funnels, and what do small under-plaques add?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.memory_hook: Preview stops, guide funnels, post speeds
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Signal-ahead and stop-ahead boards preview forced halts, lane-shrink and merge boards negotiate the funnel, and advisory plaques price the bend in safe speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: What do Divided Highway signs direct, what do curve diamonds warn of, and what do named intersection signs preview?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.memory_hook: Keep right at medians, watch junctions
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Split-highway boards order right as roads fork one-way, bend boards flag curves and narrows, and crossing boards with road names preview junctions and forced turns.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: How do advance curve signs preview bends and safe speeds, and what three facts do rectangular guide signs provide?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Signs posted before turns and curves use the arrow's shape to show what to expect and may carry a small sign below showing the maximum safe speed, while guide signs—most of which are rectangular—tell where you are, what road you are on, and how to reach destinations.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: What five road classifications can you identify from route-shield shapes and colors?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Route shields wear shapes and colors that betray their road rank, interstate, federal, state, city or county, so map-planned trips follow them true.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: How does the purpose of a yellow curve-arrow board differ from a highway route shield?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.memory_hook: Arrows preview geometry, shields map routes
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Arrow boards sketch bends with safe-speed hints while shields wear rank in shape and hue, one reading the curve and the other the map.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: How do U.S. route shields fit the shield system, and where do brown guide signs lead?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.memory_hook: Shields mark U.S. routes, brown parks
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Federal route shields repeat the rank-by-shape rule, while brown boards beckon toward parks and playgrounds.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: What do blue signs, green guide signs, and highway mileposts each show, and where do milepost numbers start?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.memory_hook: Blue services, green exits, south-west miles
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Blue squares hawk rest, fuel, camps and care, green boards aim at bike paths, lots, mileposts and chosen exits, and mile ticks march each mile from the south and west rims to reckon distances.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: What geographic features and boundaries appear on green roadside information signs?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Ever-green info boards print borders, town lines, streams, heights and landmarks of passing interest.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: What hazards do orange work-zone signs warn of, what do detour signs mark, and who holds top authority there?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Orange diamond or square work boards warn of crews, slow detours, crawling machines and shifting pavement, detour boards open the backup path, and flaggers in bright vests with paddles and red flags rule the zone absolutely.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: How do green exit signs, green info signs, blue squares, brown panels, and orange work boards divide tasks?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Green destination boards aim at exits and miles, green info boards print borders and landmarks, blue squares sell services, brown beckons leisure, and orange work boards with flaggers rule the crew zone, color sorting the errand.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: What four actions are forbidden on railroad tracks, and what blue sign sits at every grade crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.memory_hook: Never stop, shift, or race trains
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: At rails, never race the train, never strand the car astride the tracks, spare the gearshift mid-crossing, respect the deceptive bulk and pace, and note the blue round-the-clock emergency number posted at every grade crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: How does the round yellow RR sign work together with the white X crossbuck at the tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: A round yellow X with black rail initials heralds the crossing from afar, and the white crossed blades at the rails yield wheels to every train like a yield board.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: At gated railroad crossings, when must you stop, when may you cross again, and do pedestrians share the rule?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.memory_hook: Stop first flash, wait dark gates
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Where gates and blinkers guard, halt at the first flash before the arm falls, wait out the raised arm and dark lamps, never skirt the lowered arm, and walkers too must heed signals, gates, flaggers and officers.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: How do the round yellow RR sign, white crossbuck, and flashing gates escalate as you reach tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.memory_hook: Yellow alerts, crossbuck yields, gates lock
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: The yellow X warns from afar, the white crossbuck yields at the rails, and gates with blinkers jail wheels until arms rise and lamps die, three rail guards in rising command.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What updates do portable or permanent overhead message boards display, and are their directions optional?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Portable or fixed message boards broadcast traffic, weather and hazard orders along the road, and every posted direction binds the driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: At least how many coached road hours must sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds log, and how may school and home hours mix?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: Every sixteen and seventeen year old applicant must log at least forty hours of coached road training, mixing professional school lessons and home practice in any share.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What permit holding period applies to first-time adult applicants age eighteen or older before road-testing?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Adults of eighteen or more must get a learner permit and hold it at least ninety days before any road test.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Contrast the core road-test prerequisite for an adult permit holder against a teen permit holder?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Adults wait ninety permit days before the road test, whereas teens log forty road hours first, so the adult gate is time and the teen gate is practice.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: May an adult learner permit holder practice solo, or who must ride beside them?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: An adult permit holder drives only under teaching and beside a commercial or secondary school instructor or a qualified trainer of twenty plus, licensed with no suspension across four or more straight years before training.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Which adult applicants must take the eight-hour safe driving course and bring its certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Adults never licensed in Connecticut and holding no valid out of state license must take the eight hour safe driving course and show its attendance certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Which six core driving skills should you master thoroughly before showing up for your road exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.memory_hook: Speed, lanes, yielding, yellows, backing, parking
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Before testing, applicants must know proper speed, turning and driving lanes, right of way yielding, yellow light stopping, safe backing, and every style of parking including hills and curbs.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: Before shifting the test car out of park, what four readiness steps do examiners watch for?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Before moving the test car, follow directions, scan parked cars and people nearby, clear and defog glass and mirrors, and brake before shifting out of park.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: How does a passing road-test candidate handle acceleration, cruising pace, following space, and stops?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: During the drive, shift and accelerate smoothly, reach road speed promptly, keep a fitting space cushion, and stop with smooth safe braking.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: Alongside electric turn blinkers and alert corner scans, what extra signal skill must road-test takers demonstrate?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Signal every proper turn and show hand signals too, watch traffic and walkers through each turn at a fitting speed, and stay alert with sound judgment throughout.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: From cabin setup to dash icons, which seven areas does the road-test inspector grade?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.memory_hook: Setup, controls, signs, yielding, parking, dash-lights
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: The road test scores seat and mirror setup, equipment use, sign and signal response with courteous yielding, backing and parking, basic turns, warning light reading, and any extra maneuvers the inspector orders.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: When do you book your road-test appointment, and what web page lists testing offices?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.memory_hook: After time-and-training; c-t dot gov offices
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: Once the permit time and training stand met, book the road test appointment and find sites at ct.gov slash dmv slash offices.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: What vehicle condition, paperwork, and driver escort are required when arriving for your road test?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Arrive in a class fitting, mechanically safe car with valid registration and insurance papers, since an unlicensed driver may not drive there alone.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What insurance proof lets a long-term leased car take the road test—and are rental cars allowed?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A long term leased car qualifies only with insurance naming the car and the lease company registrant, and no unlicensed applicant may test in a rental.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Why might a family's leased sedan pass road-test check-in while a weekend rental car always gets turned away?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: A leased test car passes only when its insurance names car and lease company, while a rental car fails outright for any unlicensed tester.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: What happens if the inspector finds burned-out brake lights or bald tires on your test car?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: An unsafe test car cancels the evaluation and earns a free rescheduled appointment.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which documents go in your folder on road-test day, and how much is the post-pass license fee?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Road test day needs the learner permit, the CS-one eight hour course proof, an eighty four dollar license fee payable after passing, and any required medical clearance letter.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Which three training-certificate options prove road-test readiness for sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Sixteen and seventeen year olds also prove driver training with a home training CS-one, a commercial school certificate, or a secondary school certificate.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What family classroom proof must teen road-testers also document?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: Teens also prove two parent teaching hours on under eighteen law and teen driving perils, taken inside the required eight hour program.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: What course proof do every road-tester's papers share, and what two extra proofs do teens stack on?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Every tester brings the CS-one eight hour proof, but teen testers stack a second training certificate plus parent teaching proof on top.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: Which payment forms do branch offices accept, and to whom are checks made payable?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Branch offices take cash, money orders, personal checks, debit and credit cards, and bank checks, all checks payable to DMV.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: What credential do you walk out with after passing, and how soon does permanent plastic arrive?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Qualifiers leave with a temporary paper card while the permanent license card follows by mail within twenty days.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: Contrast what a newly licensed driver receives at the branch counter versus through the mail?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Qualifiers pocket a temporary paper card at the office the same day, yet the lasting plastic card travels by mail inside twenty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: During the first six licensed months, whom may a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old carry aboard?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Newly licensed sixteen and seventeen year olds carry no passengers for six months except a licensed instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, or one twenty plus person with four straight licensed years and no suspension in the prior four.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Which additional passengers unlock during months seven through twelve of a teen's license?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: In months seven through twelve the only new passengers allowed are immediate family members.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: How do Connecticut's first six teen-license months differ from months seven through twelve for siblings?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: The first six licensed months allow only an instructor, a licensed parent or guardian, or one qualified twenty plus adult aboard, while months seven through twelve add immediate family and nobody else.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Between what nighttime hours are sixteen- and seventeen-year-old drivers off the road, and which five trips are exempt?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: Teens may not drive from eleven at night to five in the morning unless riding for a job, school, worship, medical need, or as an assigned Safe Ride driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which active teen community responders are exempted from both passenger and night-curfew limits?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Active volunteer fire, ambulance and emergency medical members answering or returning from calls, plus assigned Safe Ride drivers, skip the passenger and curfew limits.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: How do ordinary teen curfew exceptions compare with the volunteer emergency-responder exemption?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: The eleven to five night curfew binds teen drivers except for job, school, worship, medical or Safe Ride trips, and a separate exemption covers volunteer crews on emergency duty.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: Which four safety, vehicle, device, and motorcycle rules bind every sixteen- and seventeen-year-old driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Permit holders and licensed sixteen and seventeen year olds must never overload seatbelts, drive public passenger or vanpool vehicles, touch any phone or mobile device even hands free, or carry motorcycle passengers within six months of endorsement.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Does passing your road test at sixteen lift the hands-free phone ban or vanpool ban?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: Overloading seatbelts, driving passenger or vanpool vehicles, touching any phone even hands free, and early motorcycle passengers are banned for both permit holders and licensed teens alike.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: What does joining the organ-donor registry cost at licensing versus changing your choice mid-cycle?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Organ donor sign up happens at licensing or renewal, online, or by mail, needs an appointment with current license or ID in hand, costs nothing, but changing the choice later needs a duplicate credential with a thirty dollar fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: For registrants age eighteen or older, what legal weight does joining the organ-donor registry carry?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: For adults of eighteen or more the donor registry counts as legal donation authorization, so tell family and read more at ct.gov slash dmv.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Contrast the fee for enrolling as an organ donor during renewal against changing that status later?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Joining the donor registry costs nothing at licensing, but flipping the donor choice later demands a duplicate credential and a thirty dollar fee.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: How soon does voter-registrar confirmation arrive after a license visit, and what happens when you change addresses?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: DMV offers voter registration or updates with every license transaction at any time, receipts and forwards the form, and a registrar confirmation should land in about three weeks, while an address change also moves the voter record unless declined.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: What connects an ordinary license address change to your town voter registration?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Voter sign up rides along any license transaction with a three week confirmation, and a plain address change moves the voter record too unless the driver opts out.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: Whom does Connecticut's limited-license program serve, and what two evaluations decide terms?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: The limited license program serves drivers whose abilities changed since licensing and newcomers who now qualify, on physician reports and possibly an inspector road skills test.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: How far ahead should applicants with stable, monitored health conditions contact Driver Services?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Stable monitored conditions may still allow driving, but affected applicants should call Driver Services at least four months early at (eight hundred sixty) two hundred sixty-three-five thousand seven hundred twenty-three.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Which license categories face tougher medical fitness standards than standard passenger drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: Health bars run higher for commercial licenses and for licenses covering taxis, delivery vans, buses and school buses.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: Which six tailored operating or equipment restrictions can a Connecticut limited license place on driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.memory_hook: Daylight, lenses, roads, automatic, mirrors, adaptive
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: A limited license can restrict driving to daylight from a half hour before sunrise to a half hour after sunset, to corrective non telescopic lenses, to ordinary highways, to automatic gears, to dual mirror cars seeing two hundred feet back, or to special control cars.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Contrast how medical rules adapt for passenger limited-license holders versus commercial and bus drivers?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Limited licenses add daylight, lens, highway, gear, mirror and equipment curbs for impaired drivers, while commercial and passenger licenses instead face tougher health bars.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Which state agency trains residents with disabilities to drive using adaptive vehicle controls?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Disabled residents who might drive with adaptive gear can seek state training through the Bureau of Rehabilitation Services at (eight hundred sixty) four hundred twenty-four-four thousand eight hundred forty-four.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: How must the parking brake, manual gearbox, and automatic selector be set before starting?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Start per the owner manual with the parking brake set, a stick shift out of gear with clutch down as needed, and an automatic selector in park.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Why must you accelerate gradually, and what does practicing clutch and throttle prevent?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Feed speed in gently since hard launches spin wheels and slide cars, and rehearse clutch and throttle so shifts neither race nor stall.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: Where do your hands belong on the wheel, and which two turning methods handle sharp corners?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Grip the wheel at eight to ten left and two to four right, hand over hand through sharp bends while straightening manually, or push pull with outward knuckles and uncrossed hands.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: How far ahead should you scan in seconds and blocks, and how do you measure it?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Scan ahead, aside and astern always, holding eyes twelve seconds out, about a city block downtown or four blocks on highways, timed by counting thousands to a fixed object.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: When do side glances matter most, and which five situations demand extra rearview mirror checks?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Favor side glances at crossings and lane moves and rear checks in dense traffic, lane shifts, slowdowns, reversing and long descents.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: How do you use a fixed roadside mark to verify you aren't outdriving your sightline?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Never outdrive vision: pick a far fixed mark and if it arrives before four counted thousands, shed speed at once.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does the twelve-second scanning rule differ in purpose from the four-second sight-distance check?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Safer drivers look at least twelve seconds ahead, about one block in city traffic or four city blocks on the highway, while the four-second sight-distance rule checks whether you are driving too fast for the distance you can clearly see.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: What checks govern entering intersections, turning left across oncoming traffic, and turning right?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Enter crossings only after left right scans, cede left turns to all oncoming traffic including bikes while rechecking twice, and turn right solely past clear lefts, clear paths, patient bikes and legal reds.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: How must you handle fresh greens, dark traffic signals, blind corners, and backed-up intersections?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Trust no signal blindly, scan even fresh greens, halt for dead lights as for stop signs, creep out past blind corners, and never strand the car blocking the box.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: What two checks apply at every railroad crossing, and what extra rule governs multi-track crossings?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Slow and sweep both rail directions at every crossing with far side room assured, and past multi track trains linger until the first clears sight of a second.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Compare the required safety checks before a left turn versus a right turn or right-on-red?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Before turning left, yield to oncoming traffic including bicycles, check that the target street is clear, and look toward oncoming traffic once more; before turning right, check left and oncoming turning traffic, check for pedestrians, never turn right immediately after passing a bicycle, and on red stop first unless a sign prohibits turning.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: Contrast your legal duty at a blacked-out signal with your safety check on a fresh green?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: A dead signal legally becomes a stop sign for all, yet even a live fresh green still demands left right scans for red runners.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: When must you stay behind the intersection line, and when should you edge forward slowly?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: Heavy traffic forbids entering without far side room to dodge gridlock, but a blind corner invites a slow edge forward so cross traffic spots the nose first.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: What colors and placements mark Connecticut work zones, and which speed limit governs inside them?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Work zones speak through orange and black roadside boards on the right, or both sides when divided, and post lower limits that rule unless absent.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: What penalties hit work-zone speeding or worker endangerment, and how do handheld phone fines change?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: Zone speeding, disobedience, lane abuse or worker endangerment can cost a thousand dollars plus points and retraining, with handheld phone fines doubled inside.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: How should you navigate shifting lanes and flaggers in work zones, especially after dark?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: Through zones slow down, heed boards and flaggers, respect shifting lanes, and drive nights with extreme care whether crews show or not.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Which merge, spacing, and patience habits carry you safely past the End Road Work sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Also watch brake lights ahead, merge early, slide from workers, shun tailgates, honor mobile crews to the End Road Work board, drop distractions, detour when able, and bank extra time calmly.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Who receives stiffer-penalty protection against careless harm, and what minimum passing clearance applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Careless harm to walkers, riders, wheelchair users, animal traffic, road crews, garbage, tank, mail and express haulers draws stiffer penalties, and every pass must leave three feet.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: How do you respond to approaching sirens and flashers versus any vehicle stopped roadside?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Sirens and red or blue flashers command a right edge stop held until passage unless officers wave on, while any roadside stop demands slowing below the limit plus one lane over when safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What gesture or movement gives a pedestrian crosswalk right-of-way, and what door check applies?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Walkers own every crosswalk, painted or sidewalk implied, once a raised hand or any body part or aid enters its mouth, and doors must never strike people, bikes or traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Do unmarked sidewalk extensions follow a weaker yield rule than painted crosswalks?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: Painted crosswalks and invisible sidewalk extensions share one rule: raised hands or entering limbs and aids all claim the right of way.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: What right-of-way rule protects pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog, even on green?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: White canes and guide dogs always win the right of way with full stops held until the road clears, greens notwithstanding at regulated corners.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: How does a white-cane or guide-dog pedestrian's priority exceed an ordinary crosswalk yield?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Ordinary walkers win crossings on intent, while cane and guide dog users win absolute held stops that outlast even green lights.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Where must you watch hardest for darting children, and which limits and signals demand obedience?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: Guard hardest for children near schools, stops, parks and ice cream trucks plus every driveway reversal, obey posted school limits, and halt for crossing pupils and guard signals.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What stop distance and crawl speed apply when passing an ice-cream truck flashing lights and signal arms?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Lit ice cream trucks with arms out force a ten foot stop fore or aft, then five mile per hour creeping yielded to crossing children, except across islands or barriers.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: What legal status do bicycles hold on narrow lanes, and why expect unpredictable moves from some riders?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Bikes count as vehicles owning lanes outright when narrow, while unskilled wobblers ignoring signs and night lights deserve widened caution.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: Where do cyclists position for straight travel, who must wear helmets, and what visibility rules apply?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: Riders keep right as safe, may hold a right turn lane left edge going straight, obey signs with hand signals, yield to walkers, helmet under sixteen, and dress bright with lights and tuned machines.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What fine penalty backs bike-yield rules, and how must you pass and maneuver afterward?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: Drivers yield to bikes at crossings, paths and pre turn cuts under doubled failure fines, pass slow with three feet minding width and loads, then avoid quick slows, stops and right hooks plus needless horn blasts.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: May you pass a cyclist in a no-passing zone, and what bike-lane and wet-weather checks apply?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: Turning drivers hunt for bikes and sidewalk children, never slice or shoulder riders off, expect wrong way wheels and sloppy wet handling, may pass safely inside no passing zones, and keep bike lanes, doors and reverse paths bike checked.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: What minimum air gap must every bike pass leave, and how do bike-yield fines compare to normal ones?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: Bike passes need three feet of air with slow care, and skipping a bike yield costs doubled fines unlike ordinary yield slips.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Contrast passing a slow bike in a no-passing zone with driving or parking inside a bike lane?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: You may pass a slow-moving bicyclist in a no-passing zone if you can do so safely, whereas stopping, parking, or driving in a designated bicycle path or lane is prohibited unless entering or leaving an alley or driveway, performing official duties, following a police officer's direction, or facing an emergency, while yielding to bicycles.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: What lane rights belong to motorcycles, and what crash share comes from cars turning left across them?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: Motorcyclists have the right to a full lane and two motorcycles may share one lane; check mirrors and blind spots by turning your head, and look carefully before turning left because about half of motorcycle crashes involve another motor vehicle and nearly forty percent are caused by that vehicle turning left in front of the motorcyclist.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: Why distrust a motorcycle's turn signal, and what following gap should you hold behind one?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Distrust lingering bike blinkers, telegraph every move, gift room for pothole dodges, trail three to four seconds or longer when wet, dip beams, and hold course while being passed.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: Contrast two motorcycles riding side by side with a car sharing a lane beside a motorcycle?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Cars must never split a lane with a motorcycle, though two motorcycles themselves may legally share one lane side by side.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: What speed marks orange-triangle vehicles, when must you yield to buses, and when may you cross double-yellow?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Expect sluggish trucks and tractors on grades, yield to signaling buses, grant orange triangle rigs under twenty five miles per hour room, and pass slow traffic lawfully even over double yellow with clear sight.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: Where do horseback riders travel, and how must motorists pass them?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: Horses travel single file rightward, and drivers must slow or halt with gentle space and silence, never horns or startling din.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: Why are a big rig's flanks and tail dangerous, and how do you stay visible behind one?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: Big rig side blind zones swallow cars unseen in driver mirrors, and tailgating their rears blinds both parties to forward trouble, so hold real following gaps.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: When is it safe to pull back ahead of a sixty-five-foot rig, and what blind distances surround wide turns?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: Sixty five foot rigs stopping on doubled room punish cut ins, so reenter only past full fronts in mirrors without slowing, and never wedge beside wide swinging turns blind twenty feet fore and two hundred aft.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: Which four physical limits constrain heavy trucks, and what danger zones must car drivers avoid?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Trucks crawl uphill, swing wide, brake long and tip tall, so human error by car drivers can still wreck the evading trucker: shun every No-Zone.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: How do you execute a legal, low-risk pass past a tractor-trailer from start to finish?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: Pass trucks solely with room sans speeding, checked mirrors, legal ground, brisk cab clearance, mirror confirmed reentry right, and sustained pace after.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: Contrast the crash trap inside a truck's front No-Zone against its rear No-Zone?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Front No-Zones punish early cut ins before whole fronts show in mirrors, while rear No-Zones punish tailgating that blinds both drivers forward.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Why do sharp curves, slick asphalt, and standing puddles all demand immediate speed drops?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Four palm-sized tire patches carry all your braking and steering force against wet pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: How should you maintain your tires, and why must speed drop on gravel or dirt?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Loose dirt and stones roll underfoot like marbles, stretching stops and kicking tails sideways.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: When must you shed speed for a curve, and what happens if you brake mid-bend?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Braking mid-corner overloads front tire traction and slides your car toward the outside shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: Why must all curve braking finish on the straightaway before turning in?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Combining cornering lean with hard brake force snaps rubber loose right inside the turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: How must every driver treat an intersection whose traffic signals have gone dark?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Blowing through unlit signal heads causes high-speed T-bones when cross traffic expects four-way stops.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: How much should you cut speed on wet pavement, packed snow, and glare ice?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Even winter treads or chains need half speed on packed snow and crawls on ice.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: What three speed reductions match wet roads, packed snow with winter gear, and ice?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Matching speed cuts to surface grip keeps stopping distance shorter than your forward sightline.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Between which exact calendar dates are studded snow tires legal in Connecticut?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Metal tire studs chew bare warm-weather asphalt outside Connecticut's strict November-to-April winter driving window.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: How do snow tires and chains differ legally from studded tires across the calendar?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Freak early snowfalls allow chains or winter rubber anytime while metal studs follow fixed dates.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Which four sneaky spots or weather moments turn roads unexpectedly icy or oil-slick?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Cold air wraps bridge decks above and below while hot-day drizzle floats buried oil.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: Why do shady hollows, bridges, melting ice near freezing, and hot opening rain slide worst?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Wet ice near freezing slides twice as slick as dry subzero ice because water lubricates tires.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: Above roughly what speed do wet tires start hydroplaning, and what makes it happen sooner?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Shallow bald grooves fail to channel water out, lifting rubber onto a frictionless wedge.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: What should your feet and hands do once your tires start hydroplaning on water?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Slamming brakes while riding water locks front wheels so touchdown yanks the car sideways.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How do preventing hydroplaning near thirty-five miles per hour and curing it afloat work together?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Dropping pace before puddles beats skimming, and lifting off throttle lets tires sink back.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: What deadly threat can aggressive driving grow into, and what mindset guards your license privilege?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Impatient tailgating or cutoffs escalate fast into violent road-rage crashes without deliberate self-control.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: Which four social and traffic factors form the first group feeding road rage?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Teens who watched parents curse traffic often copy that hostility under rush-hour pressure.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: Which four psychological traps make drivers treat lanes like personal turf and armor?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Steel cabins trick stressed commuters into feeling invincible at sixty miles per hour.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Which calm habits defuse road rage before or after another motorist cuts you off?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Assuming a sloppy lane change came from tiredness rather than malice kills anger instantly.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How should you report reckless aggression, and which roadside reactions are strictly off-limits?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Playing highway enforcer with brake-checks or chases turns one reckless driver into two.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What should you do with the keys when already angry, and how should mistakes be viewed?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Cooling down or taking a cab keeps heated emotions from weaponizing two tons of steel.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Which five obnoxious lane, signal, gesture, and horn habits spark road-rage confrontations?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Blasting the horn the instant a traffic light turns green ignites tempers for zero gain.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: What danger links left-lane camping with tailgating, and what simple habits prevent both?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Moving right for faster cars and giving three-second cushions removes highway friction.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What parking, headlight, merge, and roadway habits round out Connecticut's trouble-behavior list?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Retaliating with high beams blinds both windshields whereas dimming and adding four seconds protects you.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: When is touching the horn appropriate, and which three uses abuse it?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Horns exist solely to warn against imminent collisions rather than greeting friends or venting.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: How should you react to a hostile driver's glare, and where must you go if chased?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Locking eyes escalates confrontation, and leading a pursuer home reveals where you live.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: What two things do you deny an angry driver, and what two places offer refuge?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Refusing engagement starves road rage while police stations and crowded storefronts deter attackers.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: How should you adjust space and lane position for trucks ahead, overtaking you, or oncoming?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Speeding up beside a passing rig extends your time inside its turbulent blind spot.
sec05-card-sec05-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Extra room, ease pace, hug right

visual_sync.text_span: Extra room, ease pace, hug right

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: How many counted thousands must separate you from a truck ahead at a roadside landmark?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Riding closer than three counted thousands blinds both your forward view and the trucker's mirrors.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: What five hidden hazards punish drivers who follow a large truck too closely?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: High trailer clearance straddles road debris that smashes oil pans on close-following passenger cars.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Why do long trucks swing left before turning right, and where must you never squeeze?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Long trailer axles track tightly across inside corners and crush cars sneaking along the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: How should you respond when a large truck starts backing into a dock or driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Trying to dart behind a reversing trailer puts your roof inside a total blind zone.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: How should you handle truck blinkers, vehicles merging off ramps, and multi-lane highway entries?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Sweeping across several highway lanes in one diagonal dart blindsides fast-moving interior traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What four habits apply around trucks at rail crossings, narrow roads, busy merges, and shoulders?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Many commercial haulers must halt at railroad tracks where impatient tailgaters slam into trailers.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Which two surprising truck behaviors demand wider following distance and ban curbside right passes?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Heavy rigs can stop shorter than expected while right-turning trailers sweep clean across curbside gaps.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: How should you use an entrance ramp to join highway traffic, and what if gaps close?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Stopping at the tip of an entrance ramp forces a dangerous zero-speed merge into traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How large a time opening does a safe merge require, and why reject smaller gaps?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Squeezing into a tight gap leaves less than two seconds ahead and behind.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does the four-second merge opening compare with the normal dry-road following gap?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Merging splits four seconds between two bumpers whereas settled following guards three seconds ahead.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: Why does matching surrounding traffic speed beat weaving faster than everyone else?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Speed differences multiply lane-change conflicts while saving barely a couple minutes over an hour.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: When do you slow for a highway exit ramp versus a fast two-lane turnoff?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Holding highway pace until the exit lane prevents chain-reaction braking in through traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: What rules govern blocked intersections, narrow medians, turn signals, and railroad tracks when crossing traffic?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Pulling out solely because an approaching car blinks right causes T-bones when it drives straight.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: May you enter a backed-up intersection on green, and when is stopping halfway legal?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Blocking cross traffic on green draws a ticket, and narrow medians leave bumpers protruding.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: How do you use a roadside object to verify you are not tailgating?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Passing the shadow or signpost before finishing three thousands proves you sit too close.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Which road, weather, or vehicle conditions require stretching your gap to four seconds?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Motorcycles stop fast and trailers block sightlines, so four seconds buys essential braking margin.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: When is three seconds enough ahead, and which hazards push your cushion to four?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Adding one extra second in rain or behind blind rigs gives tires stopping margin.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: How do you manage space behind your car and safely handle a close tailgater?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Slamming brakes to punish a tailgater invites an immediate rear-end crash into your trunk.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: What two calm moves clear a tailgater safely, and which retaliatory move causes wrecks?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Coaxing an impatient driver past puts the hazard safely ahead instead of glued behind.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: How do you keep open side cushions around packs, parked doors, cyclists, and dual hazards?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Facing an oncoming truck and a cyclist together calls for slowing to handle one first.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: How should you keep yourself out of other drivers' side and rear blind spots?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Hovering off another car's rear fender hides you right when that driver changes lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Which six busy pinchpoints demand slower speeds, and where is passing strictly off-limits?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Malls, bridges, toll booths, and school zones pack unpredictable cross movements into tight lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Which three areas must you check before changing lanes, and how many lanes per move?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Scanning the far lane catches a driver two lanes over diving into the same gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: How many vehicles should you overtake per pass, and what must you scan ahead first?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Narrow bridges or pedestrians ahead force sudden swerves that erase your return space.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How many seconds and feet does a fifty-five-mile-per-hour pass take, and what if unsure?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Distant oncoming cars look stationary at highway speeds while closing a third-mile gap fast.
