sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: What mirror cue confirms you have enough room to pull back right after passing?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Never count on overtaken drivers braking to make room if you cut back early.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: What time-and-distance window starts a highway pass, and what mirror sight finishes it?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Ten clear seconds start the pass safely and two mirror headlights end it cleanly.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Why must you skip passing near intersections, rails, or shopping-lot mouths, and are shoulders legal?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Drivers pulling right out of shopping lots look left only and never expect oncoming passers.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: On highways with fewer than three lanes, when may you legally use the left lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Cruising in the left passing lane clogs flow and triggers dangerous right-side undertaking.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Which three maneuvers let drivers leave the right lane on roads under three lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Connecticut law reserves the left lane strictly for passing or preparing left-side departures.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: From which lane to which lane must turns travel before any later lane change?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Drifting wide into an outer lane mid-turn clips drivers legally turning from the opposite side.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: How do right and left turn paths differ, and how do you protect cyclists at corners?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Passing a bicyclist right before hooking right across the bike lane causes classic right-hook crashes.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Why do right turns stay curb-tight while left turns swing a wider arc?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Left feints invite curbside collisions on rights while roomy lefts let opposing left-turners pass safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Where is backing banned, how do you fix missed exits, and how do you reverse safely?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Backing down a travel lane or highway exit ramp invites catastrophic high-speed rear impacts.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: Which two maneuvers are the sole legal exceptions to Connecticut's travel-lane backing ban?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Every other missed driveway or highway ramp requires driving forward to loop back safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: How much forward sight distance do safe passes and hills require, and what do downhills need?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Checking mirrors on steep downgrades spots heavy trucks gaining runaway speed behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: How close to a blind hillcrest or curve is passing banned, and how should you picture it?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Treating every blind crest as hiding an oncoming bumper prevents gambling on hidden asphalt.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Which five road users often cannot see your car and need extra space?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Tilted umbrellas, iced windshields, and parked-car doors blind people right beside your lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: Why must drivers never read maps rolling, wear dual headphones, or rubberneck crash scenes?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Plugged ears miss sirens while staring at wrecks causes rear-end collisions with slowing leaders.
sec05-card-sec05-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Park maps, bare ears, no gawking

visual_sync.text_span: Park maps, bare ears, no gawking

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What conditions do posted speed limits assume, and what happens legally on wet, blind, or crowded roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Driving the posted maximum through heavy rain, blind sightlines, or packed traffic can still earn a too-fast-for-conditions ticket.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Why must you check your speedometer instead of relying on how fast the car feels, especially leaving an expressway?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Highway cruising numbs your sense of speed so forty-five on a local exit street suddenly feels like a crawl.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: How does driving far below normal pace affect trailing traffic, and what should a slow driver do?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Bottlenecking a line of cars tempts frustrated drivers into risky blind passes, so pull aside or choose slower streets.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How can both driving the posted speed in a storm and crawling far below traffic get a driver in trouble?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Safe pacing sits between weather hazards that demand dropping below the sign and creeping speeds that bunch traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: When you double speed from thirty to sixty miles per hour, how much does stopping distance grow?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Braking energy multiplies faster than speed, stretching stopping room past three times the thirty-mile-per-hour distance.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: On dry pavement, how many total reaction-plus-braking feet and city blocks do fifty and thirty miles per hour take?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Outrunning your sight distance means any stalled car hidden inside that full-block or half-block zone becomes unavoidable.
sec09-card-sec09-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Four hundred fifty, two hundred thirty

visual_sync.text_span: Four hundred fifty, two hundred thirty

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do stopping physics from doubling speed pair with the four-hundred and two-hundred-foot sight rules?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Connecticut test items pair triple-plus braking growth with those exact dry-road footage numbers to test safe speed choice.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What crashes do panic stops invite, and what habits keep you from needing one?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Scanning far ahead lets you lift off the throttle smoothly while still halting completely at every stop sign and line.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Does Connecticut law ever grant someone the right of way, and what duty always remains?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Insisting on your turn when another driver makes a mistake still causes a wreck you were legally expected to prevent.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Who overrides an active traffic light, and who holds priority in crosswalks and bike-path crossings?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Whether crosswalk paint is visible or implied at an intersection, pedestrians and trail users take priority over turning or through cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: What priority do pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog hold, and how must you treat your horn?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Honking startles a guide dog and scrambles the street-sound cues a blind traveler relies on to cross safely.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Who outranks electric traffic signals, and which travelers outrank everyone with horns kept silent?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Permit exams love testing these two absolute hierarchy rules side by side because neither bends for a green light.
sec09-card-sec09-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Officers top lights, canes top all

visual_sync.text_span: Officers top lights, canes top all

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: What yield rules govern driveways or shoulders, blocked intersections, overtaking cars, and signaling transit buses?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Entering an intersection without room on the far side gridlocks cross traffic, and Connecticut requires yielding to signaling buses.
sec09-card-sec09-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Side entries yield, let buses merge

visual_sync.text_span: Side entries yield, let buses merge

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Whom must left-turning drivers yield to, and whom must drivers entering a traffic circle yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Cutting across straight oncoming cars or barging in front of circulating vehicles causes angle crashes.
sec09-card-sec09-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Left yields oncoming, entry yields circle

visual_sync.text_span: Left yields oncoming, entry yields circle

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Who goes first at an unsigned intersection versus at a four-way stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: At a four-way stop, first-to-arrive rules first and the driver on the right wins only when two cars arrive together.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Whom must left turners, rotary entrants, and drivers at unsigned corners each yield to?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Keeping those three conflict directions distinct prevents hesitation and T-bone collisions at busy town junctions.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How does the right-hand rule at an all-way stop differ from the right-hand rule at a signless corner?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Using the tie-breaker rule when someone else clearly stopped first at a four-way intersection cuts off their turn.
sec09-card-sec09-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Arrival rules stops, right breaks ties

visual_sync.text_span: Arrival rules stops, right breaks ties

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Who goes first at a roundabout, how do you pick lanes and signal exits, and what is banned inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Stopping inside the circulating ring to wave an entering car in triggers immediate rear-end crashes behind you.
sec09-card-sec09-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Yield entering, signal right, never stop

visual_sync.text_span: Yield entering, signal right, never stop

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: What three rules govern entering a roundabout gap, signaling out, and keeping moving inside the ring?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Smooth roundabout flow depends on entering only real gaps, signaling right before your exit, and never braking for joiners.
sec09-card-sec09-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Gap in, right blinker, keep rolling

visual_sync.text_span: Gap in, right blinker, keep rolling

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Where are U-turns completely banned, and what sequence makes a U-turn safe where permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Checking for ban signs first, stopping with a left blinker, scanning all lanes, and finishing in the opposite right lane prevents broadside hits.
sec09-card-sec09-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Never on expressways, signal, stop, scan

visual_sync.text_span: Never on expressways, signal, stop, scan

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: What must you do when emergency vehicles approach with sirens, air horns, or flashing red or blue lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection blocks fire trucks and ambulances from turning, so clear the box first and hold at the right curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Which lanes must stop for a school bus flashing red lights, who is exempt, and when may you move again?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Only oncoming traffic separated by a physical median or barrier keeps moving; everyone else waits until lights go dark and kids reach the roadside.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: How does pulling over for an emergency responder differ from stopping for a flashing red school bus?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Responders need an open center path past right-curb cars, whereas school buses freeze whole roadways to protect crossing children.
sec09-card-sec09-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Responders right edge, bus stops lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Responders right edge, bus stops lanes

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: Who always holds the right of way where railroad tracks cross a road?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Freight and commuter trains cannot swerve and need thousands of feet to stop, so road users yield every time.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: Where should you park, how do you secure the vehicle, and which side should you exit from?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Stepping out curbside instead of into moving traffic and locking up with your keys prevents door strikes and rollaways.
sec09-card-sec09-F18.must_match_memory_hook: Off lanes, brake, curbside exit, lock

visual_sync.text_span: Off lanes, brake, curbside exit, lock

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: Which direction should you turn your front wheels when parking on a hill in Connecticut?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Aiming tires sharply toward the curb or road edge guides any brake failure away from live travel lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What extra wheel step distinguishes hill parking from standard flat-ground curb parking?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Flat parking sets brake, gear, and close curb alignment, while hills add angled front tires so gravity never pulls into traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Which roadway spots, structures, lanes, and clearance zones forbid parking in Connecticut?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Blocking crosswalks, ramps, hydrants, tunnels, tracks, double-parked lanes, or disabled bays without a permit risks towing and safety hazards.
sec09-card-sec09-F20.must_match_memory_hook: Skip crossings, hydrants, bridges, bike lanes

visual_sync.text_span: Skip crossings, hydrants, bridges, bike lanes

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What are Connecticut's exact parking distances for stop signs or safety zones, fire hydrants, and the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Memorizing twenty-five feet, ten feet, and within one foot nails three of the highest-frequency numeric test questions at once.
sec09-card-sec09-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Twenty-five stop, ten hydrant, one curb

visual_sync.text_span: Twenty-five stop, ten hydrant, one curb

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: When must headlights run besides night, what is the wiper rule, and can you drive with parking lights alone?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Connecticut law requires full headlights whenever wipers run, at dusk, or driving away from a low blinding sun.
sec09-card-sec09-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Wipers require headlights, never parking lamps

visual_sync.text_span: Wipers require headlights, never parking lamps

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: When should you use high beams, and which traffic or weather conditions require dropping to low beams?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: High beams reflect off rain, snow, and fog droplets straight back into your eyes and blind oncoming or leading drivers.
sec09-card-sec09-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Empty dark highs, traffic storms low

visual_sync.text_span: Empty dark highs, traffic storms low

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: How should you respond if an oncoming driver leaves high beams on, and what must you never do?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Blasting your own brights back creates two blinded drivers closing at highway speed.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How do empty dark roads, fog or traffic, and stubborn oncoming high beams each set your headlight choice?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Pairing beam etiquette with right-edge eye tracking keeps night visibility sharp without blinding anyone.
sec09-card-sec09-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Highs solo, lows crowded, never retaliate

visual_sync.text_span: Highs solo, lows crowded, never retaliate

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: How far do high beams reach, what speed does that cap, and what if storms cut sight to two hundred feet?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Because fifty miles per hour needs four hundred feet to stop, driving faster at night outruns your headlights, and dense storms call for pulling off.
sec09-card-sec09-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Four hundred feet caps near fifty

visual_sync.text_span: Four hundred feet caps near fifty

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: When does a polite light horn tap fit, and when should you sound a sharp warning blast?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Matching horn force to urgency alerts drifting cyclists or drowsy drivers gently while reserving sharp blasts for sudden collision threats.
sec09-card-sec09-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Light tap warns, sharp blast rescues

visual_sync.text_span: Light tap warns, sharp blast rescues

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What type of Connecticut license is Class D, and which vehicles may an unrestricted holder operate?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Standard passenger cars, pickups, and vans fall under Class D until commercial weight or passenger thresholds apply.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Which separate Connecticut handbooks cover commercial truck-and-bus drivers versus motorcycle endorsement applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Air-brake rigs, buses, and two-wheeled motorcycles carry specialized physics and laws beyond standard passenger rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: How does the Class D passenger handbook divide territory from Connecticut's truck-bus and motorcycle manuals?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Studying the right manual ensures you prep for your exact vehicle class before booking an exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: Which official Connecticut web address hosts current laws, required document checklists, and knowledge-test booking?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Checking c-t dot gov slash d-m-v beforehand prevents wasted trips with missing identity paperwork.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: What is the leading cause of death for ages fifteen to nineteen, and when does new-driver crash risk peak?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Crash odds stay elevated across the first two licensed years and spike sharpest right after passing.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Until what age range is the brain's risk-judgment center still developing—and how does that affect teen drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Incomplete prefrontal wiring makes fast highway gaps look safer to a teenager than to experienced adults.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: How does carrying teen passengers change crash odds, and what role belongs to parents at home?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Every added teen peer multiplies distraction and show-off pressure inside a rookie driver's car.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What two nighttime dangers explain why families and police enforce Connecticut's young-driver curfew?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Late-night fatigue stacks onto reduced headlight sightlines right when rookie experience is thinnest.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: How do teen seat-belt habits compare with other ages, despite what buckling up prevents?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Clicking a three-point belt takes two seconds yet cuts fatal ejection and trauma dramatically.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: What alcohol standard binds teen drivers, and how much alcohol starts hurting driving skill?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Even a single drink dulls rookie coordination and spikes crash probability under twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which everyday inside-the-cabin distractions lift serious crash risk according to Connecticut's manual?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Calls, texts, rowdy friends, dial hunting, and unrestrained pets all steal eyes and attention.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: What credential is mandatory before any behind-the-wheel practice begins—and on every practice drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Practicing in an empty lot without your physical learner permit aboard still violates state law.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: How old must you be to apply for a Connecticut learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Connecticut starts passenger learner permits at birthday sixteen rather than age fifteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: How does a newly qualified applicant receive their Connecticut photo learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Verify your mailing address carefully on your application so your photo card arrives cleanly.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: What health standard applies to permit seekers, and what happens if a risky medical condition exists?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Clearing medical review before practice starts protects both the student driver and everyone sharing roads.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: Which office should an applicant facing possible medical review contact well ahead of applying?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Reaching Driver Services weeks ahead avoids delays while doctors submit medical forms.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: How long does a Connecticut learner permit remain valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Whichever milestone arrives first—passing your road test or hitting two years from issue—ends the permit.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: Contrast how a fast-moving student's permit ends versus an unhurried learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Waiting past twenty-four months forces re-applying before you can legally practice or road-test.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: What consequence can hit a learner who ignores passenger, supervisor, or curfew permit rules?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Losing your permit mid-training resets momentum and delays earning your Class D license.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Which two tests must every applicant pass to earn a Connecticut learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Both eyesight standards and handbook knowledge must clear before your permit can issue.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: How do you schedule and pay for the knowledge exam, and when does road-test booking unlock?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Walk-in knowledge testing isn't offered—reserve online first, pass, and only then book your road exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: How many questions appear on Connecticut's knowledge test, and how many right answers pass?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Missing more than five handbook questions misses eighty percent—drill sample items beforehand.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: Keep Connecticut's two knowledge-test numbers apart: total questions asked versus minimum right answers?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Mixing up test length with passing score trips nervous test-takers on exam rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: Can acing all twenty-five written questions earn a permit if your vision screening falls short?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Sharp rule recall never substitutes for seeing signs and pedestrians clearly down the block.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: What visual acuity applies across license classes—and what extra field requirement applies with sight in one eye?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Glasses or contacts may help reach twenty-forty, while single-eye drivers also prove wide side awareness.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does Connecticut's vision screening add an extra check for applicants blind in one eye?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Peripheral breadth in the working eye compensates for losing binocular coverage on the blind side.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What risk do you run at a traffic stop if you drive without corrective lenses listed on your card?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: When lenses helped pass your eye screening, wearing them behind the wheel is a legal restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: How often does Connecticut's manual recommend visiting an eye specialist, and why?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Distance vision fades gradually enough that drivers rarely notice blurry signs without an exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: Where must your supervising instructor sit, and what legal responsibility do they share?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Sitting right beside the wheel lets an alert coach intervene early and co-own safe operation.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Outside formal school lessons, who is the single person a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old permit holder may carry?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: That lone supervisor must be twenty-plus with four straight suspension-free licensed years—zero friends aboard.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: Under what sole training setup may extra student companions ride with a teen permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Professional commercial or high school driver-ed cars often rotate two or three students with an instructor.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: Which family members—meeting the twenty-plus, four-clean-year rule—may home-train a teen, and who serves as backup?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Only when no parent, guardian, grandparent, or spouse qualifies may an aunt, uncle, sibling, or stepparent teach.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: When does a qualified twenty-plus family trainer count as the lone legal passenger for a teen permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Sleeping or scrolling in the passenger seat violates the active-instruction duty of a learner drive.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: Which mandatory course must first-time Connecticut license seekers of every age complete, and where?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Even brand-new thirty-year-old applicants take the eight-hour Safe Driving Practices class before licensing.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: Which three driver-training pathways can prepare a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old for licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Even home-coached teens still attend an approved school for the eight-hour course with parent hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: What mandatory classroom commitment falls on a teen permit holder's parent or guardian?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Bringing parents in covers teen curfews, passenger bans, and crash risks so home rules stick.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Which adult or teen applicants must complete the eight-hour Safe Driving Practices course?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Only drivers transferring a valid out-of-state adult license or holding prior Connecticut licensure skip it.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: How many classroom and road hours make up full school driver-ed, and what certificate unlocks testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Earning certificate c-s-one proves both classroom theory and forty-plus coached hours are complete.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: Which certificate covers a home-trained teen's eight-hour class, and what topics fill its hours?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: At least four hours target alcohol and drug dangers while two hours train the parent or guardian.
sec01-card-sec01-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Form c-s-one-a; four alcohol, two parent

visual_sync.text_span: Form c-s-one-a; four alcohol, two parent

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: How does certificate c-s-one differ in purpose from certificate c-s-one-a?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Bringing the wrong certificate to your road exam stalls check-in because each tracks a distinct syllabus.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: Which five items does a home teacher formally sign off on the learner permit for road-test day?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Home training demands thirty study hours, full manual review, forty road hours, and the eight-hour parent-included course.
sec01-card-sec01-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Thirty study, eight-class, manual, forty-road, parent

visual_sync.text_span: Thirty study, eight-class, manual, forty-road, parent

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: If a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old moves to Connecticut already licensed elsewhere, must they still take the eight-hour class?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Out-of-state teen licenses do not waive Connecticut's eight-hour Safe Driving Practices requirement under eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: How many permit days must formal driving-school graduates wait before road-testing versus home-trained applicants?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Structured school instruction shaves sixty calendar days off the standard six-month learner wait.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: What exact classroom-and-professional-road hour combination unlocks the shorter one-hundred-twenty-day road-test wait?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Logging those eight behind-the-wheel hours specifically with a licensed school instructor triggers early eligibility.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Can pure home training ever qualify for Connecticut's one-hundred-twenty-day road-test waiting period?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Every non-school applicant waits the full one hundred eighty days past permit issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: How do total required teen road hours compare with the professional road hours that unlock the one-hundred-twenty-day wait?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Even after thirty classroom and eight pro hours unlock day one-twenty, teens still complete forty total road hours.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Why are brakes uniquely vital, and which four warning signs demand an immediate mechanic visit?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Because nothing else stops your vehicle, ignoring spongy pedals or pulling brakes turns routine traffic into a runaway hazard.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: How soon must you visit a repair shop if steering feels stiff or responds late?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Driving even one more trip with delayed or binding steering leaves you unable to dodge sudden lane hazards.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: What mechanical problem causes repeated bouncing or wheel-wrestling after hitting bumps?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Worn shock absorbers let tires hop off pavement over bumps, slashing steering control and extending stopping distances.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Which exterior lights must work from outside the car, and what headlight flaw needs repair?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Dashboard indicators miss burned-out bulbs or misaligned beams that blind oncoming traffic on dark two-lane roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: What four visibility steps prepare your windows, wipers, and windshield before driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Peephole scraping or hazy inner glass hides pedestrians and cross traffic the moment sunlight glares across your windshield.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What is the sole legitimate purpose of your vehicle's horn?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Treating the horn strictly as a safety alert rather than an anger vent keeps urgent warnings unmistakable.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Where do you find proper tire pressure, and when must you inspect tires for wear?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Test writers love pairing sidewall maximums as a trap—always match the manual or door-jamb spec using a gauge.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: How do you run the penny tread check, and what shows safe depth?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Testing the shallowest groove catches uneven wear before rain turns bald rubber into a hydroplaning ski.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: In the penny tread check, contrast a partly covered Lincoln head against tread below that mark?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Once all of Lincoln's head shows, shallow grooves cannot channel water or slush away during wet braking.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: Which maintenance schedule does every driver owe their vehicle, and why?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Skipping routine inspections invites highway breakdowns or sudden mechanical failures right inside fast traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: What five problems can a neglected engine cause, and how do you prevent them?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Losing engine power mid-merge or stalling across an intersection puts you directly into high-speed collision paths.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Why are exhaust leaks deadly, and what three habits protect riders from fumes?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Carbon monoxide has zero smell or color, knocking occupants unconscious before anyone notices cabin air turning toxic.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: How many days do you get to repair and retest a vehicle after failing emissions?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Letting that two-month repair window expire blocks registration renewal and risks compliance penalties.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Which greenhouse gas comes from burning fuel, and how can car shoppers and drivers cut it?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Comparing economy labels before buying and easing off aggressive throttle cuts both tailpipe carbon and fuel bills.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: What legal trouble can aftermarket window tint or custom lighting swaps trigger?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Darkened glass or nonstandard bulbs may look sharp online yet violate Connecticut equipment statutes on public roads.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: What insurance rule governs registered cars, and what sequence follows an unanswered lapse warning?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Ignoring a motor vehicle agency warning notice escalates a fixable compliance fine into suspended plates and an illegal-to-drive car.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: After an insurance lapse, contrast the first warning option with what happens if you ignore it?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Opening state mail promptly lets you settle a lapse agreement before registration cancellation parks your vehicle.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: When do you adjust seat and mirrors, and how do you verify side-mirror aim?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Swinging side mirrors outward until your car's flank barely shows when leaning forward shrinks dangerous blind zones.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Why must you secure loose items and keep cabin floors clear before rolling?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: A rolling water bottle wedged behind your brake pedal can block emergency stopping when milliseconds count.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Who must buckle up in Connecticut before moving, and why don't airbags replace seat belts?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Front airbags cushion forward hits only, leaving unbelted riders unprotected in side impacts, rear-enders, or rollovers.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: How must two-piece belts and motorized shoulder belts be worn to protect you?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Skipping the manual lap belt with motorized shoulder straps lets crash forces submarine your body under the dash.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: Which cabin zones do airbags shield, and which crash types still rely on seat belts?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Seat belts anchor you upright behind the steering wheel during swerves, side collisions, rear impacts, and rollovers.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: If both driver and passenger ride unbuckled, how are citations and fines issued?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Adult passengers carry personal legal accountability in Connecticut, meaning one traffic stop can write multiple seventy-five-dollar citations.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which age group must every driver ensure is buckled, and who gets cited when unbuckled?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Checking every buckle before shifting out of park prevents avoidable tickets and protects young passengers.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Do an unbelted driver and passenger split one ticket, or get cited individually?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether belt fines are pooled—every unbuckled person receives an individual ticket and fine.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: What restraint rules govern children under age two or thirty pounds versus ages two to five or under forty pounds?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Rear-facing cradles fragile infant necks, while five-point harnesses distribute crash forces across stronger toddler bones.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Which seats fit kids five to eight or forty to sixty pounds, how do split cases resolve, and what airbag ban applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: A deploying front airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing infant shell with fatal force.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: Which age and weight cutoffs separate mandatory rear-facing seats from forward-facing harnessed seats?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Both milestones—age two AND thirty pounds—must be reached before turning a harnessed child seat forward.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Compare restraint rules for five-to-eight or forty-to-sixty-pound kids versus eight-plus and sixty-plus, including split cases?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: If a seven-year-old already weighs sixty-five pounds, split-case rules still keep them in a booster or harness.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: How quickly do seat belts unlatch, how rare are fire or water crashes, and how do belts aid escape?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Unbelted riders get knocked unconscious against cabin glass, whereas belted survivors stay alert to unclick and climb out.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: Why does staying belted beat being thrown clear, and which direction do side-struck riders slide?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Being hurled onto asphalt or under traffic is far deadlier than riding down impact inside your safety cage.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Where and at what posted speed limits do most fatal crashes happen?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Skipping belts on quick grocery runs ignores where over half of fatal collisions actually strike.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: What real-world impacts match the force of a twenty-five-mile-per-hour head-on crash?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: No human arms can brace against three-story fall physics—only locked seat belts hold your body back.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: Which two twenty-five-unit facts crush the excuse of skipping belts on short local errands?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Local errands sit right inside the deadliest radius, and neighborhood speeds already carry three-story drop forces.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: When are handheld devices banned, where may drivers call freely, and how do adult and teen rules differ?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Red-light stops still count as highway operation—pull safely onto a parked shoulder before touching any screen.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: Does waiting at a red light lift the phone ban, or must you park safely roadside first?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Checking messages at a stoplight draws the exact same citation as texting at highway speed.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: How does hands-free calling legality differ between adult drivers and sixteen- or seventeen-year-olds?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Speakerphone and dashboard Bluetooth do not shield sixteen- or seventeen-year-old drivers from Connecticut's total device ban.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Which emergency calls may any age driver place, and which on-duty responders may use handhelds?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Dialing police, fire, ambulance, hospitals, clinics, doctors, or dispatch stays legal whenever real emergencies strike.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: What three consequences hit an under-eighteen driver convicted of a cell-phone violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: One quick text under eighteen triggers license suspension upon conviction plus mandatory operator retraining.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Contrast a teen dialing emergency help with a teen making a casual call while driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Connecticut protects genuine crisis calls at every age while punishing casual teen phone use with suspension.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: How does Connecticut define distraction, and how can eyes, hands, or thoughts trigger crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Daydreaming drivers stare straight through red brake lights without mentally registering danger ahead.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: How does mental distraction hide compared with taking eyes off road or hands off wheel?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Passengers spot phone scrolling immediately yet never notice a driver mentally zoned out.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Who bears legal blame when an inside-the-car distraction causes a collision?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Blaming a ringing phone, spilled drink, or noisy passenger never excuses the driver legally.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Why does crash fault land strictly on the wheel-holder rather than on a cabin distraction?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Every licensed operator accepts legal command over everything happening inside the vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which everyday items, screens, passengers, or habits create cabin distractions?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Reaching down for a dropped item steals both forward sight and steady wheel control.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Which seven outside-the-window sights lure drivers' eyes away from traffic?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Turning your head toward flashing cruisers or billboards blinds you to sudden lane halts.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How do interior cabin traps contrast with exterior roadside traps?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Presetting cabin gear before driving handles inside lures while steady self-discipline defeats roadside rubbernecking.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: What pre-drive and cabin habits neutralize distractions before you shift into gear?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Settling routes, climate knobs, snacks, kids, and pets while parked frees attention for traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Which clues reveal a distracted driver nearby, and how much room should you give?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Drivers scrolling or arguing drift across lane lines without touching turn blinkers first.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does managing your own cabin differ from defending against distracted neighbors?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Order inside your car prevents self-inflicted errors while scanning spots erratic neighbors early.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Why must you keep three to four seconds back and pass distracted leaders warily?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Unaware drivers rarely check mirrors before swerving back toward the center of lanes.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: How does physical or mental fatigue impair a driver much like alcohol or drugs?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Exhaustion dulls vision, speed sense, and temper before dropping drivers asleep at highway pace.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Which four driver groups face sharply elevated risk for drowsy-driving crashes?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Teens need extra sleep while untreated apnea and graveyard shifts multiply nod-off danger.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: By how much do untreated obstructive sleep apnea and night-shift work multiply wheel-sleep risk?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Fragmented daytime rest and interrupted breathing leave drivers exhausted long before eyelids feel heavy.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: What sleep bank, break interval, passenger help, and medication rule prevent highway fatigue?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Stopping every hundred miles or two hours with a relief driver beats marathon tiredness.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: Which four preparation pillars protect drivers before starting a long road trip?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Combining full pre-trip rest, two-hour stretch stops, shared driving, and zero sedatives keeps minds sharp.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: What physical and driving warning signs tell you drowsy nodding has begun?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Cranking loud music or rolling windows down proves drowsiness already compromised safe driving.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: Once yawning, daydreaming, or lane drifting starts, what is the only safe response?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Willpower never stops microsleeps once your brain starts shutting down behind the wheel.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: How do short parked naps, two-cup caffeine timing, and midnight-to-six hours fit fatigue defense?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Caffeine wears off fast while body clocks plunge deepest between midnight and six morning.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: How does pairing two coffees with a fifteen-to-twenty-minute nap compare against true sleep?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Two coffees before a twenty-minute nap buy temporary alertness, yet only sleep cures exhaustion.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: What pattern marks typical drowsy crashes, and what must you do after hitting rumble strips?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Drowsy drivers drift solo off highways at full speed without touching brakes once.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: How do colds, pain, or store-bought and prescription drugs affect driving, and what should you do?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Everyday decongestants and painkillers slow reaction times enough to turn minor colds hazardous.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How do worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness affect driving, and how do you counter them?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Rushing while upset tempts darting lane changes unless you cool down or ride passenger.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: What actions match hitting rumble strips, feeling sick, taking sedating meds, or feeling upset?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Recognizing when your body, medicine cabinet, or mood compromises safety prevents solo crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What share of fatal crashes involves alcohol, and why are new drivers hit harder than veterans?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Beginners still concentrate consciously on steering and braking, so even one drink wrecks coordination.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which four financial, legal, and personal losses hit drivers caught driving after drinking?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: One impaired drive triggers courtroom fines, skyrocketing insurance bills, license loss, and jail.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: What brain function does alcohol numb first, and why does the manual compare overdrinking to sunburn?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Because self-judgment goes numb first, drinkers feel fine until impairment passes safe return.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: Which six core driving abilities deteriorate further as blood alcohol climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Blurred sight, sluggish feet, and warped distance judgment turn routine intersections into traps.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What is Connecticut's safest rule on drinking and driving, especially for drivers under twenty-one?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Even small amounts trigger impairment arrests, and one drink can bust underage drivers.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Which three standard pours equal one drink, and why are exotic mixed drinks tricky?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Tall fruity mixed cocktails mask multiple liquor shots inside a single deceptively sweet glass.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How do liquor, regular beer, and wine servings match up against fancy mixed cocktails?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Counting glasses fails completely when one specialty cocktail packs three standard drinks.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Why do coffee, cold showers, exercise, and fresh air fail, and what sobers you?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Black coffee and cold water only produce a wide-awake, shivering impaired driver.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: What is the sole factor that clears alcohol from your bloodstream?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Your liver oxidizes alcohol on a fixed biological clock that workouts never accelerate.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What two smart transport plans bring everyone home safely from parties with alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Picking a zero-alcohol driver or booking transit ahead prevents impaired midnight decisions.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Which four common prescription or over-the-counter medicines can impair driving like alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Store-bought allergy tablets sedate vision and reflexes just as heavily as prescription drugs.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: What must you check before driving on medication, and why never combine pills with alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Combining sedatives with liquor multiplies impairment instead of merely adding effects together.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: How do cold, headache, allergy, or nerve drugs act solo versus combined with alcohol?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Synergistic drug-alcohol reactions can trigger blackouts behind the wheel or life-threatening overdose.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Which three chemical samples can officers require, and what minimum suspension and interlock follow failure?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Court penalties stack atop the Commissioner's mandatory forty-five-day suspension and ignition interlock.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: What minimum suspension and ignition-interlock term hit a driver of any age who refuses chemical sampling?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Refusing breath, blood, or urine sampling doubles minimum interlock time from six months to one year.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How does minimum ignition-interlock time compare between failing a chemical sample and refusing one?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Both trigger forty-five suspended days first, yet refusal doubles the mandatory interlock period.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: What blood-alcohol threshold, locations, and penalties govern Connecticut's under-twenty-one zero-tolerance law?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Parking lots and private driveways carry the exact same underage arrest power as highways.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Where does Connecticut enforce its two-hundredths-percent underage limit, and what penalty follows?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Sitting behind the wheel at two-hundredths percent in a private lot still brings interlock.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Which five conviction categories suspend sixteen- and seventeen-year-old driving privileges in Connecticut?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Even unlicensed teens lose future licensing eligibility when convicted of these five offenses.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What suspension terms and restoration fee hit first versus repeat teen restriction violations?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Every teen reinstatement demands a one-hundred-seventy-five-dollar fee on top of court fines.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: How does Connecticut measure the suspension length for a repeat teen restriction violation?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Younger sixteen-year-olds caught twice stay suspended clean through their upcoming eighteenth birthday.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: How long are the first, second, and third teen cell-phone or texting suspensions, plus restoration fee?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Touching a phone at sixteen or seventeen triggers an immediate thirty-day first suspension.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: What suspension ladder and restoration fee hit teens convicted of speeding twenty or more over?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: First-offense teen speeding twenty-plus over doubles the opening phone suspension to sixty days.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How does the opening teen phone suspension compare with twenty-over teen speeding across three strikes?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Both ladders match at ninety days second and one hundred eighty days third.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What suspension and jail exposure hit teens on first versus repeat GDL or reckless counts?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Repeat teen reckless convictions jump to full one-year suspensions and one-year jail ceilings.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What suspension and jail exposure apply to first and repeat teen street-racing convictions?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Even a first street-racing conviction exposes teen drivers to a full year locked up.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: How does maximum first-offense jail time compare between teen reckless counts and street racing?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Connecticut punishes organized street racing twelve times harder in maximum first-offense jail exposure.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Which three severe charges bar drivers under eighteen from youthful-offender status?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Adult criminal records attach when underage drivers flee serious-injury crashes or drive impaired.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: Which five youthful-offender findings still get reported to DMV for license suspension?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Youthful courtroom status never hides reckless, racing, or police-eluding adjudications from DMV.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How do Connecticut's three youthful-offender bars contrast with its five DMV-disclosed youth adjudications?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Fatalities, serious-injury flight, and DUI block youth status completely while five lesser offenses trigger DMV suspensions.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: How must you park and behave inside your car during a Connecticut police stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Keeping doors shut, dome light on at night, and hands visible calms dark stops.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Where is the proper venue to contest a traffic citation you believe is unfair?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Arguing on the shoulder never voids a ticket and only escalates roadside tension.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How many moving or suspension convictions trigger operator retraining at twenty-four-and-under versus twenty-five-plus?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Younger drivers hit mandatory attitude-and-safety retraining one ticket sooner than older motorists.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: Which three teen violations trigger retraining, including what rule on hands-free phones under eighteen?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Drivers under eighteen cannot legally use even hands-free mobile devices behind the wheel.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: What penalty hits if a retrained driver picks up another moving violation within three years?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Three probation-style years follow retraining where a single moving ticket suspends privileges.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: How do Connecticut's age-based retraining thresholds combine with the three-year post-course rule?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Knowing two counts through twenty-four, three at twenty-five-plus, and thirty-day post-school suspensions nails retraining.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: Why should you signal every turn or lane change even when the street looks completely empty?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: The traveler you failed to spot in a driveway, blind spot, or shaded sidewalk needs your blinker most.

visual_sync.text_span: Signal every move, unseen eyes watch

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: How many seconds ahead must you start signaling, and why wait until passing intervening driveways or side streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Signaling before an earlier driveway tricks a waiting driver into pulling out right in front of your car.
sec10-card-sec10-F02.must_match_memory_hook: At least three seconds, pass driveways

visual_sync.text_span: At least three seconds, pass driveways

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: When another car waits to pull out between you and your upcoming turn, when should you flick your signal on?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Blinking early makes that driver think you are turning before reaching them, inviting a broadside pull-out crash.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How do Connecticut's three-second minimum warning and the rule on nearby driveways work together?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Good signaling balances giving trailing cars three seconds notice without misleading side-street drivers ahead of your turn.
sec10-card-sec10-R01.must_match_memory_hook: Three seconds minimum, clear earlier drives

visual_sync.text_span: Three seconds minimum, clear earlier drives

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: Why must you check your dashboard blinker indicator after finishing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Soft steering angles often fail to trip the auto-cancel switch, leaving a stray blinker that misleads surrounding traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: What false message does an uncancelled turn signal send after a soft lane change or curve?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Drivers waiting at the next corner may pull across your nose believing your leftover signal promises an immediate turn.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How many times should you tap the brake pedal before an unexpected slowdown, and what spots call for it?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Flashing your brake lamps before lane-free highway exits, pre-intersection parking, or hidden hazards wakes up following drivers.
sec10-card-sec10-F05.must_match_memory_hook: Tap brakes three or four times

visual_sync.text_span: Tap brakes three or four times

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: How should brake-light warnings differ between a routine slowdown and a surprise stop?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Reserving three or four quick flashes for unannounced halts makes urgent warnings stand out from everyday traffic braking.
sec10-card-sec10-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Steady for expected, taps for surprise

visual_sync.text_span: Steady for expected, taps for surprise

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: If mechanical trouble strikes, what steps come first, and where must you avoid stopping if stuck on the roadway?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Stopping just beyond a hilltop or blind curve hides your disabled vehicle until approaching cars are right on top of you.
sec10-card-sec10-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Pull off, flashers, keep long sightlines

visual_sync.text_span: Pull off, flashers, keep long sightlines

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: How do you warn traffic behind a stalled car with or without flares, and what lane mistake is forbidden?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Changing a flat tire or standing inside an active travel lane turns a simple breakdown into a fatal pedestrian strike.
sec10-card-sec10-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Flares behind, white cloth, off lane

visual_sync.text_span: Flares behind, white cloth, off lane

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: What sequence can stop your car safely if the service brakes suddenly fail?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Pumping may rebuild hydraulic pressure, while easing the parking brake without locking rear wheels and downshifting scrubs off speed safely.
sec10-card-sec10-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Pump pedal, ease parking brake, downshift

visual_sync.text_span: Pump pedal, ease parking brake, downshift

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: How should your hands and feet respond when a tire suddenly blows out or goes flat?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Stomping the brakes during a blowout pitches weight onto the shredded tire and spins the car out of control.
sec10-card-sec10-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Grip tight, lift gas, light brake

visual_sync.text_span: Grip tight, lift gas, light brake

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: How does your brake-pedal action during brake failure contrast with your brake-pedal action during a tire blowout?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Mixing these two emergencies up on test day or the highway is dangerous because hard braking ruins blowout stability.
sec10-card-sec10-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Pump dead brakes, spare blown tires

visual_sync.text_span: Pump dead brakes, spare blown tires

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: What happens to steering and braking if your engine dies while moving, and how do you pull off?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Power assist vanishes when the engine stalls, but mechanical steering and brakes still work if you muscle them firmly.
sec10-card-sec10-F10.must_match_memory_hook: Heavy wheel, press brake very hard

visual_sync.text_span: Heavy wheel, press brake very hard

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What steps should you take if your headlights suddenly go dark at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Hazards, turn signals, or fog lights help guide you onto the shoulder where you stay parked until headlights work.
sec10-card-sec10-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Slow gently, pull off, flick switch

visual_sync.text_span: Slow gently, pull off, flick switch

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: What is the safest sequence if your engine suddenly races on its own with a stuck accelerator?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Shifting to neutral disconnects the racing engine from the wheels immediately while keeping power steering and brakes alive until parked.
sec10-card-sec10-F12.must_match_memory_hook: Eyes forward, shift neutral, pull off

visual_sync.text_span: Eyes forward, shift neutral, pull off

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Why must you never turn the ignition key to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Once the steering column locks mid-roll, you cannot turn the wheels to follow a curve or reach the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What three collision-avoidance actions can dodge or soften almost any impending crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Fixating only on the brake pedal overlooks open lanes or forward gaps that could clear an impact completely.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: In what crash scenario is pressing the gas pedal your smartest escape, and what comes right after?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Surging into clear pavement ahead pulls your cabin past a red-light runner or skidding rear car before you ease back down.
sec10-card-sec10-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Side or rear threat, open ahead

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: Among the three collision-avoidance options, what exact combination of threat direction and road space calls for speeding up?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Accelerating never helps a blocked front hazard, so reserve throttle escapes strictly for side or rear hits with open lane ahead.
sec10-card-sec10-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Rear or side threat, clear front

visual_sync.text_span: Rear or side threat, clear front

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: How must you use the brake pedal during an emergency stop in a vehicle with antilock brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Lifting your foot when the ABS pedal shudders or buzzes shuts down the rapid computer pumping that keeps steering alive.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: How do you make the fastest emergency stop in a car without antilock brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Threshold braking just short of lockup stops shortest, and quick lift-and-repress cycles unlock skidding tires.
sec10-card-sec10-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Squeeze hard, lift at skid, repeat

visual_sync.text_span: Squeeze hard, lift at skid, repeat

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: How does emergency hard-stop footwork differ between antilock brakes and conventional non-ABS brakes?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Pumping ABS wastes stopping distance, while pinning non-ABS locks the tires into a straight, uncontrollable slide.
sec10-card-sec10-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Pin ABS down, modulate plain brakes

visual_sync.text_span: Pin ABS down, modulate plain brakes

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Why can steering beat braking at highway speed, how do you hold the wheel, and what does ABS allow?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: At speed you need far less distance to steer clear than to halt, and ABS lets you brake and steer simultaneously.
sec10-card-sec10-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Turns quicker, both hands, ABS steers

visual_sync.text_span: Turns quicker, both hands, ABS steers

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: Without antilock brakes, how do you combine braking and steering, and why choose off-road over oncoming lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Releasing the brake unlocks front tires so they bite into the turn, and grass or bushes beat a fatal head-on impact.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: What separates steering during an emergency stop with antilock brakes versus without them?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Locked non-ABS front wheels slide straight ahead regardless of how far you turn the steering wheel.
sec10-card-sec10-R06.must_match_memory_hook: ABS steers braking, plain releases first

visual_sync.text_span: ABS steers braking, plain releases first

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: What triggers a tire skid, and why is preventing one far better than trying to recover?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Once ice, water, or excessive corner speed breaks tire traction, steering and brake inputs lose authority until grip returns.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: If your car starts skidding, what should you do with the brake and steering wheel until straight?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Counter-steering smoothly as the tail swings back prevents a violent fishtail whip into the opposite ditch.
sec10-card-sec10-F21.must_match_memory_hook: Stay off brake, steer target, unwind

visual_sync.text_span: Stay off brake, steer target, unwind

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Why must your feet lift off the pedals while your hands steer and counter-steer in a skid?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes locks sliding tires harder, whereas rolling wheels regain directional grip where your hands point them.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: What restraint protects occupants best in any crash, and what emergency gear belongs in the vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Buckled lap-and-shoulder belts keep every rider inside the safety cage, while flares, first aid, and tools handle the scene.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: How should you position your body, head, and foot right before being struck from behind?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Resting against the head restraint limits whiplash, and pinning the brakes stops the impact from shoving you into cross traffic.
sec10-card-sec10-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Press back, headrest, stand on brakes

visual_sync.text_span: Press back, headrest, stand on brakes

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: Why do seat belts matter critically in a side-impact collision where front airbags cannot help?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: A broadside hit throws unbuckled drivers across the cabin away from the steering and brakes needed against a second hit.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: If a frontal collision cannot be avoided, why aim for a glancing blow and rely on your belts after the airbag?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: Deflecting energy off-center beats a dead-square wall hit, and airbags deflate immediately while belts hold through secondary impacts.
sec10-card-sec10-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Angle glancing blow, belts guard second

visual_sync.text_span: Angle glancing blow, belts guard second

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: How do survival actions differ across rear, side, and unavoidable frontal impacts?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Each crash vector throws energy differently, combining seatback-and-brakes behind, belt retention sideways, and angled deflection ahead.
sec10-card-sec10-R09.must_match_memory_hook: Rear brakes, side belts, front glance

visual_sync.text_span: Rear brakes, side belts, front glance

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: When should you stop at someone else's crash, and why must uninvolved drivers never slow to stare?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Gawking clogs lanes needed by ambulances, fire engines, police, and tow trucks while sparking secondary rear-end crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What legal duties bind any driver involved in a collision, including hitting a parked car or injury crash?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Leaving any collision scene early, even an unattended fender-bender, turns an accident into a hit-and-run crime.
sec10-card-sec10-F23.must_match_memory_hook: Stop immediately, locate owner, call police

visual_sync.text_span: Stop immediately, locate owner, call police

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: What five steps prevent fires, electrocution, and secondary crashes at a collision scene?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Leaking fuel vapors plus hot ignitions or cigarettes ignite fast, and downed power lines can energize pavement and metal.
sec10-card-sec10-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Clear lanes, ignitions off, set flares

visual_sync.text_span: Clear lanes, ignitions off, set flares

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: How should you prioritize and treat injured crash victims while waiting for medics?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Moving spine-injured victims without fire or traffic danger risks paralysis, silent non-breathers need help first, and liquids choke shock victims.
sec10-card-sec10-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Do not move, breathing, bleeding, warmth

visual_sync.text_span: Do not move, breathing, bleeding, warmth

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: What details must you exchange after a crash, how do you handle an unfound parked-car owner, and when must police be notified?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Complete driver, vehicle, witness, and insurance records plus required police reports for injury, death, or property damage protect you legally.
sec10-card-sec10-F30.must_match_memory_hook: Swap full details, note, report damage

visual_sync.text_span: Swap full details, note, report damage

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: At a collision, when may victims be moved, when must you stop, and when must officers be called?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Every involved driver halts every time, victims move only for fire or traffic peril, and police handle injuries, deaths, or broken property.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: What five lane-control tasks do pavement markings handle along the street?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Painted lines and symbols organize passing, lane changes, turn pockets, stop bars, and pedestrian walkways even without signs nearby.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Which roadway edges do solid white edge lines and solid yellow edge lines each mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: Spotting yellow on your right instead of your left on a divided highway instantly warns you entered the wrong way.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: What color separates lanes moving the same direction, and how do dashed white and solid white differ?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Solid white channel lines discourage lane hops near busy weave zones, intersections, or tunnels unless special need arises.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: How can you tell traffic direction immediately just from whether a lane divider is white or yellow?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Checking center-line color after turning onto an unfamiliar road in rain or night glare confirms whether adjacent traffic meets you head-on.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Between two same-direction lanes, what changes for lane changers when dashed white becomes solid white?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Making your lane choice while dashes remain avoids cutting across solid white bars right at the intersection throat.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: What do yellow center lines divide, when does a dashed yellow line allow passing, and what do yield lines mark?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Single opposing lanes separated by dashed yellow open safe passing, while painted yield lines mark mid-block crossings where walkers win.
sec11-card-sec11-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Opposing lanes, dashed passes, yield pauses

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: When a dashed yellow stripe runs alongside a solid yellow stripe, which direction is allowed to pass?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Crossing when the solid stripe sits nearest your lane puts you into a blind hill or curve sightline.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: What is the only legal reason to cross twin solid yellow center stripes on a two-way road?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Overtaking slower traffic across double solid yellow is illegal both ways, whereas turning left into driveways or alleys remains lawful.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: Between a lone dashed yellow center line and solid yellow center lines, what grants permission to pass?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Yellow color tells you traffic opposes you, while broken dashes versus solid paint decide whether overtaking is open.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: How does a mixed solid-and-dashed yellow center pair differ from double solid yellow stripes?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Mixed center paint opens passing for one clear-sight direction, whereas twin solid stripes restrict both directions to left turns.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Where must you halt for a required stop, whom must you yield to at crosswalks, and why watch unpainted corners?

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: How do stop lines and crosswalks work together at intersections, including corners with no crosswalk paint?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Halting behind the white stop bar preserves buffer space before both marked zebra stripes and unmarked intersection crossings.
sec11-card-sec11-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Stop behind bar, yield all crosswalks

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: How are restricted lanes marked, and who qualifies for transit, bicycle, and HOV diamond lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: Driving solo in a white-diamond carpool lane or drifting through a bus or bike lane brings steep restricted-lane fines.
sec11-card-sec11-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Signs and diamonds reserve special users

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What do diagonal stripes, hazard funnel lines, double solid white, painted curbs, and sharrow bike chevrons each indicate?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Reading specialty markings keeps you out of fixed-object gores, no-swap double white zones, fire lanes, and close bicycle conflicts.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How does a lane painted with a white diamond differ from a lane painted with a bicycle sharrow?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Permit questions love contrasting exclusive diamond lanes against open travel lanes where sharrow chevrons remind cars and cyclists to share.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: What maneuvers use a shared middle lane, what paint borders it, and how can rush hour change it?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Solid outer yellow with inner dashed yellow frames shared left turns and legal U-turns, though overhead signals can flip some reversible.
sec11-card-sec11-F09.must_match_memory_hook: Both ways turn left, check rush

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: What pavement lines edge a reversible lane, and what do green arrow, red X, blinking yellow X, and steady yellow X mean?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Ignoring a red X or lingering under a steady yellow X puts you nose-to-nose against reversed commuter flow.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: How does a shared center left-turn lane differ in purpose and flow from a reversible travel lane?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Cruising straight in a two-way turn lane is unlawful unless rush-hour lane-control lights convert it into a one-way reversible lane.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: Which active teen community responders are exempted from both passenger and night-curfew limits?

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: How do ordinary teen curfew exceptions compare with the volunteer emergency-responder exemption?
